indicators.text: Explore the planting and harvesting methods used for different species of crop.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain which fertilizers and chemicals are used for specific crops in an operation and the impact that those choices can have on future cropping decisions (e.g., herbicide carryover and what environmental conditions can affect this).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the finances of a crop operation including seasonal and foreign workers, buying or leasing equipment, accessibility to markets, cost of input, crop insurance, cash advance programs, risk management tools such as crop insurance and AgStability and expected revenue.

outcomes.statement: Prepare a management plan for an operation of one or more specific species of crop.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18B: Crop Management Plan (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 7C, 10C and 18A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify specific crops (e.g., wheat, canola, lentils, fruit, vegetables and forage) for a farm operation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of a two-year, three-year, four-year and longer crop rotation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the influence of soil types, land features and climate on the choice of crop rotation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the buildings and equipment required for a chosen crop production operation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the farming cycle date ranges for a chosen crop rotation (e.g., impact of spring and fall frost dates and the reasons for the order of crops in the rotation).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify planting methods for crops in a rotation (e.g., air seeder, planter and specialized seeder for forage crops).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify harvesting methods for crops in a rotation (e.g., swathing, baling, green chopping and straight cutting) and the advantages and disadvantages of using crop desiccation products.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain which fertilizers and chemicals can be used for a chosen crop rotation.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the process, advantages and disadvantages in applying chemicals (e.g., pre-plant, pre-emergence and post emergence) and fertilizers (e.g., broadcast, seed placed, mid row and side banded) to chosen crops.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze the finances of a crop operation including seasonal workers, buy or lease equipment options, accessibility to markets, cost of input, cash input advances, crop insurance, forward contracting, the risks versus the advantages of forward contracting and expected revenue.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the implications of climate change (e.g., drought, deluge and storms) on the growth, harvesting and yield of crops.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Prepare an effective time management schedule that balances farm time with school, recreation and work and considers seasonal time management differences.

outcomes.statement: Prepare a management plan for an operation involving one or more specific crop and livestock species.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Multi-product Management Plan (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 17A and 18A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the benefits (e.g., grain to feed livestock, manure to fertilize crops and financial coverage when one operation is less successful) of having crop and livestock production in the same operation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the role of livestock in a mixed operation (e.g., nutrient cycle, feeding crops to build organic matter in soil and livestock grazing for weed control).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify one or more species of crops (e.g., wheat, barley, canola, lentils, fruits and vegetables) and livestock (e.g., cow/calf, dairy, equine, pork, bison, egg production and bee keeping) that are suitable for a mixed operation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the annual and production cycle date ranges for chosen crop and livestock species.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the structures (e.g., buildings, fences and corrals) and land (e.g., land features including soil types and use of that land) needed for a chosen mixed operation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze the suitability of farm locations (e.g., soil type, landforms and climate) for a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate livestock management practices (e.g., percentage as meat processing, crossbreeding and introduction of new animals), the handling of manure as fertilizer and herd protection measures (e.g., herd dogs, donkeys and structures).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a livestock nutrition program for a chosen multi-product operation, including the use of crops for feed, feed storage, method of feeding, grazing methods and sources of water.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify planting and harvesting methods for the crops grown in a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the crop rotation best suited for a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Identify the fertilizers and chemicals to be used for crops in a chosen multi-product operation.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss the financial considerations needed for a chosen multi-product operation including human and equipment resources, types of products, seasonal and foreign workers, buy or lease equipment options, outsourcing stages, accessibility to markets, cost of input, grazing / harvesting restrictions associated with specific chemicals that are used in weed, insect and disease control for crops and expected revenue.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Prepare an effective time management schedule that balances farm time with school, work and recreation and considers seasonal time management.

outcomes.statement: Explore transportation regulations including the movement of farm equipment and livestock on public roads.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: Transportation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the licensing, insurance and operator's qualifications for handling different types of farm equipment on private land and public roads.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the Ministry of Highways requirements (e.g., permits, restrictions such as width-height-length and weight, lighting, slow moving signs, clear visibility rules and escort vehicle requirements) to transport farm equipment, livestock and grain on provincial highways and roads.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the implications that seasonal road restrictions have on a farming operation (e.g., marketing and labor requirements).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the requirements or exemption status for agricultural equipment and vehicles in the transportation of dangerous goods.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine provincial and federal livestock transportation regulations (e.g., types of trailers, food and water requirements, manifest and the amount of time livestock can be hauled).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of a transportation logbook.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: List examples of tools and emergency equipment required on farm machinery while in transport on a public road.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the dangers of overhead power lines when moving farm equipment.

outcomes.statement: Examine animal breed characteristics and development.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21A: Animal Breeds (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the proper terms for the gender of livestock animals (e.g., steer, heifer, colt, filly, hen and ewe).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the main distinguishing physical characteristics (e.g., age, frame, size and weight) of an ideal specimen of a chosen livestock breed.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify qualities (e.g., age, health and undesirable physical characteristics) to be considered when culling livestock from a specific type of livestock operation (e.g., beef breeding and dairy farms).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Summarize the relationship between purebred breeders and commercial operations.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of expected progeny differences (EPD) when breeding cattle.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the introduction of new livestock to the prairies by early settlers.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the development of desired characteristics of livestock through breeding practices of the First Nations and Métis peoples and early settlers.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the benefits of crossbreeding.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: List the strengths and weaknesses of several breeds of a chosen livestock species.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Classify breeds of a chosen livestock species according to their purpose.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explore the codes and practices for a chosen livestock species.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Investigate organizations that maintain a breed registry in Canada.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Discuss the development of exotic livestock (e.g., ostrich and llama) farming in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Explore how horses were introduced to First Nations peoples and why they are important to their culture.

outcomes.statement: Examine animal breed behaviours.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21B: Animal Breed Behaviours (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 21A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore behaviours of livestock including herd instinct, characteristics of the social hierarchy in a herd and flight distance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe basic livestock needs (e.g., comfort, reproduction, exercise, food, communication, survival and protection).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how livestock respond to various stimuli (e.g., response [positive], reaction [negative], acceptance and tolerance) in their environment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how a handler should react to livestock responding to specific stimuli (e.g., moving to different surroundings, loud noises, changes in weather and dogs).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and explain possible causes of vices (e.g., teeth grinding, rearing, biting and difficulty in catching).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate handler techniques designed to minimize risks to animal and worker health and prevent injuries.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how to handle different animal breeds according to their behavioural characteristics.

outcomes.statement: Explore safe methods of working around, and handling, livestock under stress.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22A: Basic Handling - Stress (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 21A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the effects of stress in livestock on their health and production.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize the characteristics of an animal under stress (e.g., agitated or aggressive behaviour and flight risk).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how a handler's body language (e.g., aggressive behaviour) affects livestock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the use of safe handler behaviours (e.g., slow movements, calm tone of voice, avoid cornering livestock and maintaining an escape route) when approaching and working with livestock under stress.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate and explain how to approach an animal safely using ground manners (e.g., scope of vision).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a plan for handling livestock experiencing stressful situations (e.g., injured animal and death of the queen bee) and emergency situations (e.g., barn fire and livestock struck by vehicle).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the accepted methods for properly euthanizing livestock in the least painful and most humane way.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the benefits of proper bedding and housing design (e.g., stall size, hive structure, base, floor grooving, scratchers and location of waterers) on animal comfort.

outcomes.statement: Investigate safe methods of restraining, moving and transporting livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22B: Basic Handling - Restraint, Movement and Transportation · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 22A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore organizations (e.g., 4-H clubs) that teach proper handling of livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the use of basic restraints (e.g., halter, stocks, cage and pharmaceuticals).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss methods of catching a difficult animal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Catch, halter and lead an animal safely.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe an animal's expected behaviour in various situations (e.g., being led, tying, grooming, bathing, clipping, crutching and mother-baby interactions).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how to appropriately manage unwelcome behaviours (e.g., halter pulling, biting, kicking and striking).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the balance points of a chosen species of livestock.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe preparation, loading and unloading procedures.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain how to recognize and use flight zones when handling livestock.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Compare different types of trailers (e.g., straight haul, angle haul and open stall) and their purpose.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss the characteristics of animals that are not fit for transport.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe how to transport a sick animal.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Explain how to use animals (e.g., horses and dogs) and vehicles (e.g., plane, helicopter, ATV and trucks) to move livestock.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Investigate how technology (e.g., drones) can be used to manage livestock.

outcomes.statement: Explore the regulations governing handling and treatment of livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22C: Basic Handling – Regulations (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 22B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe acceptable and unacceptable aspects of livestock management, such as principles of punishment and reward and physical and psychological abuse.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the laws governing improper treatment of animals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research regulations governing enclosure size for specific types of livestock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine moral issues of the use of tools that cause pain (e.g., electric cattle prods, whips and electric fences) in livestock handling.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the role of the Animal Protection Service of Saskatchewan (APSS).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore codes of practice (e.g., Code of Practice for the Care and Handling of Beef Cattle by National Farm Animal Care Council [NFACC]) in the handling of specific livestock.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research the use of Saskatchewan Premises Identification (PID).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the importance of traceability of livestock (e.g., source of transmissible contamination like E. Coli and proving organic status of meat).

outcomes.statement: Explore safe and humane methods of euthanizing livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22D: Basic Handling - Euthanasia (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 20 and 22B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze the protocol (e.g., animal is to be relocated, euthanized or marketed) for conditions or diseases for which treatment is unsuccessful using regular efforts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore common untreatable diseases (e.g., rabies, bovine spongiform encephalopathy [BSE] and avian influenza) that may result in euthanizing an animal.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how to protect humans and herds from transmissible diseases.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Evaluate situations (e.g., broken leg, end of life cycle and suffering) in which euthanasia may be necessary.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine acceptable and unacceptable methods of euthanizing animals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore situations (e.g., infectious disease) in which a veterinarian may be required to perform euthanasia.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe acceptable methods of carcass disposal.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the factors affecting livestock nutrition.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23A: Livestock Nutrition (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify common food sources (e.g., hay, grain, forages and additives) for a specific livestock species and their role in the livestock's diet.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare feed storage options.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess hay quality based on a list of criteria (e.g., quantity of stems or seed, color and odour).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the importance and methods of feed testing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze different livestock watering methods.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the importance of proper feeding routines (e.g., time of day, frequency and locations).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe physiological responses to changes in feed (e.g., colic and founder).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss problems associated with inadequate nutrition and insufficient water intake.

outcomes.statement: Investigate livestock nutritional requirements.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23B: Livestock Nutrition Requirements (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 23A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define feed terminology such as total digestible nutrients, protein content, energy, trace minerals, crude protein, crude fat and feed supplements.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Read and interpret feed labels.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the basic nutritional requirements of various livestock according to breed, age, gender, time of year, reproductive cycle and physical condition.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the importance of calculating dry matter and using a scale to feed animals a specific weight of feed.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the water requirements of livestock, including factors that may affect these requirements (e.g., animal size, growth stage, temperature and humidity).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how feed concentrates, supplements and creep feeding can be used to meet an animal’s unique needs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss why a salt block is used in livestock nutrition.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the advantages and disadvantages of commercially prepared feeds.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the proper mixture of prepared food for nutritional value for a specific purpose (e.g., maintenance, growing and fattening).

outcomes.statement: Apply understanding of nutrition to livestock feeding programs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23C: Livestock Feeding Programs (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 23B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the function of parts of the digestive system and the concept of rumination in specific livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of different types of feeding systems.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Investigate support programs for managing livestock feeding.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and use feeding and nutritional records.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Determine the cost of feed (e.g., hay, grain and supplements) for one animal of a specific type of livestock, for one year.

indicators.label: g

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate the proper use of livestock handling equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24A: Livestock Handling Equipment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the safe operation of large handling equipment (e.g., squeezes, head gates and chutes) to prevent animal and worker injury when moving livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the types and operation of different gates to manage the movement of livestock.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Practise proper use of hand-held tools (e.g., prods, whips and control poles) for managing livestock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the use of animal identification equipment (e.g., brander, tagger and microchips).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use small equipment (e.g., shears, hoof trimmer and grooming gear) to care for livestock.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare equipment used for handling large (e.g., cattle, horses and bison) and small (e.g., pork, chickens and sheep) livestock.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Perform cleaning and sanitizing procedures of livestock handling equipment.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the use of scales to weigh different types of livestock.

outcomes.statement: Explore the equipment used for feed, water and waste in livestock production.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24B: Livestock Feed, Water and Waste Equipment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate the ability to read and interpret controls, gauges and indicators commonly found on feed, water and waste equipment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the common types of feeding systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the components and operation of feeding equipment (e.g., silos, augers, feed carts, feed rollers, mechanized conveyors, liquid feed systems and hay feeders).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the operation of feed milling and processing equipment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the components of a water supply system including pressure pump, tanks with controls, filtration system and distribution.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research various waste management systems (e.g., manure sweeper, manure spreader, compost pile, manure pit and lagoon) used in livestock production.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the environmental and safety issues associated with waste disposal.

outcomes.statement: Explore the function of specialized equipment used in livestock operations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24C: Specialized Equipment for Livestock (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the function of equipment used in the honey extraction process (e.g., scratcher, de-capping tool, extractor, separator, settling tanks, pumps, melter).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the importance of specialized equipment (e.g., piglet heating equipment, ventilation and cooler systems) in a swine production facility.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the ban of gestation crates in Canada.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function of equipment (e.g., milking machine, pasteurizers, separators, homogenizers and tanks) used in the milking process in dairy farming.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the tools (e.g., clippers, shears, carding paddles, roving machine) used to shear sheep and turn their fur into yarn.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the function of equipment (e.g., incubators, hatchery equipment, egg transfer machines, slaughter equipment) used on a fowl farm and/or egg production facility.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the individual mechanical components (e.g., rollers, motors) in feed mills.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the equipment used to remove animal waste from housing facilities and spreading or injecting the waste as fertilizer.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the assessment of livestock health.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25A: Livestock Health Care - Assessment (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore welfare assessment tools as recommended by the Canadian Council on Animal Care (CCAC).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform an evaluation of an animal's vital signs including temperature, pulse and respiratory rate and recognize when additional care may be required.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of common livestock injuries, disorders and diseases.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess livestock injuries, disorders and diseases to determine if veterinary care is required.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the recognition and significance of conformation faults and blemishes in livestock.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate how body condition scoring is used to assess the health of different types of animals.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe livestock dental and hoof issues that require treatment.

outcomes.statement: Explore the cause, treatment, management and prevention of livestock injuries, conditions and diseases.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25B: Livestock Health Care - Injuries, Conditions and Diseases (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 25A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of biosecurity in ensuring herd health and production.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe mitigation strategies to prevent new livestock from introducing diseases to a farm.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the contents of a basic first aid kit and the general equipment (e.g., pails, stomach tubes and blankets) used to treat injured animals.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the cause, treatment and prevention of injuries (e.g., sprained joints and impaled objects) and open wounds.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research common conditions such as influenza (e.g., bird and swine flu), African Swine Fever and food-borne illnesses (e.g., Escherichia coli and Salmonella).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify common symptoms, nature and the precautionary measures to prevent a chosen disease.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the identification and management of genetic deformations (e.g., mule foot, cleft pallet and beak deformity) in livestock.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the causes and treatment of gastro-intestinal conditions (e.g., consuming foreign objects, bloat and constipation).

outcomes.statement: Investigate the use of medication in treating livestock.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25C: Livestock Health Care - Medication (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 25B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the medical treatment of common diseases (e.g., white muscle disease, bovine black leg and foot rot) in livestock.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the function and use of anaesthetics, antibiotics and vaccines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship between drug withdrawal time and maximum drug residue limits in the body or products of an animal (e.g., milk, eggs and honey).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research Health Canada regulations that prescribe acceptable residue levels of medication in livestock and livestock products.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze the storage, handling and disposal of medications in a drug protocol and medication program for a livestock operation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the manufacturer's specifications for dosage of medications to ensure optimum effectiveness.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine treatment options to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain why different injection sites are used for vaccines and antibiotics.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify the location on an animal to administer a particular antibiotic or vaccine.

indicators.label: j
k
indicators.text: Investigate the economic considerations of using medications (e.g., medication cost versus value of animal).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of maintaining livestock health history records.

outcomes.statement: Explore production of livestock products in Saskatchewan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26A: Livestock Products - Production (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 8

indicators.text: Identify animal products (e.g., eggs, milk, honey, wool and meat) produced in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the quality grades (e.g., choice, standard and utility) used for meat products.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the variation in terminology for specific cuts of meat in different livestock in the American system and other cultures.

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain why different breeds of a species of livestock are used for different purposes (e.g., wool versus meat sheep, milk versus beef cattle and egg laying versus meat chickens).

indicators.text: Describe equipment (e.g., egg packer, milking machine and honey extractor) used for a specific livestock product.

indicators.text: Explain the rationale and process of a breeding program.

indicators.text: Describe the methods for controlling animal breeding (e.g., castration and separation of males from females).

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III - Occupational Health and Safety in n The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019.
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse - work that you believe is unusually dangerous

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one's performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Examine the relationship between stewardship and sustainability.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Stewardship and Sustainability (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define the term sustainability.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and components of each of the four pillars of sustainability (i.e., social, human, economic, environmental).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe what sustainability means in agriculture.

outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 10

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III - Occupational Health and Safety in n The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019.
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse - work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one's performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on basic strategies to interpret American Sign Language messages.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on basic metacognitive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- construct a plan for new learning tasks with the guidance of the teacher;
- reflect on the communication process by checking copied signing for accuracy; or,
- keep a learning log to gain awareness of which language learning strategies are most effective.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on basic interactive and affective strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- seek the assistance of a friend to interpret text;
- repeat what someone has signed to confirm mutual understanding; or,
- recognize common facial expressions as part of ASL communication.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on basic interpretive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- replay familiar self-chosen recorded video texts to enhance understanding and enjoyment;
- use gestures, illustrations and contextual clues to aid comprehension of unfamiliar signs; or,
- endeavour to read finger-spelled words as whole units rather than letter by letter.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on basic strategies to begin expressing oneself in American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on basic cognitive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- identify similarities and differences between aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- imitate signed words and sentences; or,
- memorize new sign vocabulary by repeating it or signing/finger-spelling it.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on basic interactive and affective strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- recognize and respond to turn-taking cues;
- check with peers or teacher regarding accuracy of sign choice and production; or,
- experiment with basic forms of expression in simple conversations and note their acceptance or non-acceptance by more experienced signers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on basic productive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- increase signing vocabulary by copying what others sign, practising signs that are visible in the immediate environment and using resources;
- supplement signed communications with a variety of non-verbal cues (e.g., mime, pointing, gesturing, drawing pictures, illustrations, dramatization); or,
- apply knowledge of iconic signs that look like their intended meaning (e.g., eat, drink, sit) to communicate meaning by experimenting with other similar iconic signs.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on a variety of strategies to interpret American Sign Language messages.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on a variety of metacognitive strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- make a plan in advance about how to approach a language learning task;
- reflect on the communication process, including attending and signing, by checking copied signing for accuracy and monitoring own sign production to check for persistent errors; or,
- keep a learning log to evaluate own performance and identify which language learning strategies are most effective.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- work with a friend to identify patterns and relationships in signs;
- summarize the point reached in a discussion to help focus the talk and ask follow-up questions to check for understanding; or,
- recognize facial expressions as an essential component of ASL.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on a variety of interpretive strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- view a variety of video recordings to ensure exposure to regional, cultural and gender signing variations;
- use knowledge of the context to aid comprehension and ask for things to be repeated in order to understand complex ideas; or,
- mentally prepare questions and make predictions about new information based on prior knowledge and personal experience.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on a variety of strategies to express oneself in American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on a variety of cognitive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- compare and contrast aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- group together sets of signs (vocabulary, structures) with similar characteristics; or,
- make information easier to understand and remember by using reference points and initiatives like classifiers and body shifts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- work cooperatively with peers in small groups to rehearse or role-play language use;
- assess feedback from conversation partner to recognize when the message has not been understood (e.g., squinted eyes, blank look, head shake) and start again using a different tactic when communication breaks down; or,
- use new signs which occur in conversations, making use of them as soon as appropriate and asking for confirmation that a form used is appropriate.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on a variety of productive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- apply knowledge of sentence patterns and ASL structure to form new sentences;
- employ circumlocution and definition to compensate for gaps in vocabulary; or
- practise facial expressions, movement, location and non-manual signals (e.g., facial expressions, mouth morphemes, head nod/shake, shoulder shift/contrastive structure/spatial organization) to assist in effective communication.

Use and assess a variety of cognitive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- assess similarities and differences between aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- group together sets of signs (e.g., vocabulary, structures) with similar characteristics and use induction to generate rules governing language use; or,
- make information easier to understand and remember by using reference points and initiatives like classifiers and body shifts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and assess a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- participate cooperatively in conferencing, brainstorming and debating and invite others into the discussion;
- initiate or maintain interaction with signers who are deaf, deafened or hard of hearing; or,
- use a range of fillers, hesitation devices and gambits to sustain conversations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and assess a variety of productive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- employ rhythm and symmetry in signs and use familiar patterns appropriate for various genres;
- revise and improve expressive communications by using knowledge of patterns and structures in ASL to form new sentences; or,
- rephrase difficult structures or strategically use circumlocution to clarify communication.

indicators.text: Research local arts communities (e.g., collectives, arts advocacy groups, funding organizations).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Build and share understanding of the value of building communities through the arts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a community, in own classroom, through a shared focus.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the purpose of arts organizations in supporting communities of artists (e.g., CARFAC, Listen to Dis’, OSAC, SK Arts, SaskCulture).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the social, economic and personal benefits of belonging to arts communities.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss ways to engage and sustain communities through the arts (e.g., How can we honour existing connections? How can we bring families into the school and share learning with others?).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Design, plan and carry out a student-created arts collective (e.g., storyteller collective, visual art collective).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Generate inquiry questions to explore big ideas such as:
- engagement (e.g., how to involve families, outreach).
- connecting and sharing and teaching talents within the students’ own world.

outcomes.statement: Create an arts expression to challenge, reinforce or draw attention to ideas or societal norms.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate ideas for investigation and examine how various artists have responded to those ideas.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how arts expressions evolve and influence societal norms (e.g., artists as agents of social change).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research Indigenous artists whose work challenged or challenges the norms of a particular time and place (e.g., treaty education outcome HC12 - examine how treaties within contemporary society impact on individual’s lives).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Propose and create an arts expression to draw attention to a concern or idea of personal interest.

outcomes.statement: Examine how learning gained through the arts may be transferrable to careers and personal pathways.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on and discuss transferable skills (e.g., communication, digital skills, collaborative processes, creative problem solving, self expression, empathy, innovation, being able to construct).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compile and share a creative portfolio (e.g., an organized collection of work showcasing one’s creativity, abilities and thinking skills).

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of networking including how to find collaborators and support other artists and arts communities.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on own life goals and assess how one’s creative skills could be applied in various fields.

outcomes.statement: Examine and express how the arts provide opportunities to learn about oneself.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on own art works and personal growth.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Construct assessment criteria and set goals for own work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Document own progress.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Invite feedback from peers (e.g., dialogue, personal responses).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Plan ways to share own work and make connections with community (e.g., class, school, external groups).

outcomes.statement: Investigate how the arts engage people holistically, including physically, spiritually, intellectually and emotionally.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the holistic nature of the arts and the benefits to wellbeing and mental health (e.g., connect with teachers, community leaders, artists, Elders, online experts, counsellors).

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Investigate how artists reveal connections of body, mind and spirit through their practices.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss examples of First Nations and Métis arts expressions that engage people physically, spiritually, intellectually and emotionally (e.g., treaty education outcome SI12 - investigate the values and beliefs of self, family, community, and society in relation to the importance of honouring the spirit and intent of treaties).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on connections between own arts expressions and the spiritual, physical, emotional and intellectual domains (e.g., How does my work connect to one or more domains?).

outcomes.statement: Investigate contemporary arts practices as a response to place and time.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate inquiry questions to help develop understanding of what contemporary practice means (e.g., What is contemporary arts practice?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Examine the work of artists who respond to contemporary social issues as potential points of inspiration such as:
- How are artists responding to current social justice issues (e.g., marginalization of newcomers, bias or hatred based on race or gender and sexual diversity, economic inequities, environmental and social sustainability)?
- How do First Nations and Métis arts expressions reflect historical and contemporary concerns (e.g., treaty education outcome TPP12 indicator - examine the importance of decolonization as a process that supports the understanding that We Are All Treaty People.)?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Respond to site-specific arts expressions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate immersive and interactive arts (e.g., moving from place to place, non-traditional performance and exhibition spaces, virtual spaces).

outcomes.statement: Apply injury prevention principles to ensure safe work performance in the autobody trade.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1A: Injury Prevention (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE), including dust masks, approved respirators, coveralls, chemical resistant gloves, eye and hearing protection and footwear.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify, label, store and handle hazardous materials according to Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS 2015).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess the fire plan for the work area, including components such as fire alarms, fire extinguishers, exits and procedures, and make recommendations for improvements.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess hazards and apply appropriate safety procedures when working in a confined space.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Disconnect batteries and other power sources prior to undertaking autobody repairs where appropriate.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage as a result of unsafe work acts or environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the proper procedures to follow to report a workplace injury.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply safe and fair work practices, including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the ergonomic design of the work space and implement appropriate procedures to ensure safety.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Implement a plan for a safe and healthy classroom and shop environment.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of automobile design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Automobile Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of automobile design from various eras and places and discuss characteristics of selected models.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify major (e.g., roof, floor, quarter panels, cowl section and rocker panels) and minor (e.g., front fenders, hood, trunk lid, door and splash pans) exterior automobile body components.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare body-on-frame, unibody and modified unitized automobile body construction.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how different types of glass (e.g., laminated and tempered) are designed to prevent injuries to automobile occupants.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research required qualities and skills necessary to design automobiles.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine how financial considerations can impact automobile design.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the effect of relevant federal legislation and regulations (e.g., safety) on automobile design.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create, using drawing skills, computer-aided design programs or model-making, an innovative automobile body considering factors such as safety, fuel efficiency, occupant comfort and ride, ergonomics, automobile use and styling.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain autobody hand tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Hand Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how to use hand tools such as wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, body hammers, chisels, dolly blocks, files, pulling tools, picking tools and hand cutting tools safely.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform correct procedures for a specific autobody repair using appropriate hand tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect hand tools before use and tag for repair as required.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain and store hand tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the cost of purchasing hand tools to enter the autobody trade.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent work-related injuries from the improper use of hand tools.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain autobody power tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Power Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how power tools such as grinders, drills, drill presses, nibblers, die grinders, cut-off wheels, files, featheredgers, ratchets and impact wrenches safely.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform correct procedures for a specific autobody repair using appropriate power tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect power tools before use and tag for repair as required.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain and store power tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the cost of purchasing power tools to enter the autobody trade.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent work-related injuries from the improper use of power tools.

outcomes.statement: Use gas metal art welding (GMAW) equipment to complete specified autobody welds.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5A: Welding in Autobody (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate knowledge of GMAW equipment such as nozzles, contact tips, liners, wire rolls, gauges and flow meters, amperage adjustment and voltage adjustment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the importance of employing correct start-up and shut-down procedures for GMAW equipment including checking and cleaning up the work station.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare various types of wire and shielding gases used for GMAW.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Disassemble, clean and reassemble GMAW welder components.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify metals and perform preparation and assembly tasks prior to welding.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform and analyze a variety of specified welds, including plug weld, spot weld, butt weld and lap weld.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the purpose and proper use and fit of personal protective equipment (PPE) required for welding, including eye protection (lens shades), clothing, hearing protection and footwear while identifying the hazards from which they protect individuals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Ensure all PPE is cleaned appropriately.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to straighten metal.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Metal Straightening (Core) · Suggested Time: 20-30 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the range of corrective work procedures required to straighten metal.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate technical measurements to prepare a surface for repair.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Examine metal to detect how stretched areas feel and look, and determine how to shrink the areas.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the metal to know where to shrink and how much to shrink, and use appropriate tools to shrink the areas.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research, estimate and compare the repair cost to straighten metal versus replacement.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when straightening metal.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to body fill.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Body Filling (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare cost estimates of the materials used to repair damaged surfaces.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate how much body filler and hardener is needed to repair damaged surfaces.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Rough areas to be filled with disc sanders using a 60-or 80-grit disc to ensure the body filler will adhere to the metal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to spread body filler over damaged areas with putty knives to create a smooth appearance similar to finished panels.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply appropriate sanding techniques to prepare surfaces for refinishing and to obtain true panel contours.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine damaged areas for smoothness and adjust as necessary to obtain true panel contours.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures by wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as a particle mask, eye and ear protection and rubber gloves and cleaning as appropriate.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when body filling.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research short- and long-term health concerns related to body filler particles and dust in the workplace.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to flat surfaces.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Flat Panel Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 4 and 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare cost estimates of the materials used for repairing flat surfaces that have rust damage.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate areas to be cut out for flat panel repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to measure areas to produce replacement panels.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Construct repair patches and apply correct welding procedures (e.g., lap joint or butt joint, spot or plug weld).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Select appropriate tools and procedures to prepare work areas for filling.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine patches to ensure repairs are ready for refinishing and painting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures for welding and using cut-off wheels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss how repairing rust damage contributes to environmental sustainability.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when repairing panels.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to contoured surfaces.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Contoured Surface Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 4 and 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare cost estimates of the materials used for repairing contoured surfaces.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate areas to be cut out to do contoured panel repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Demonstrate how to measure areas and transfer to metal panels, including:
- shaping metal panels to the contour of the areas being replaced;
- constructing repair patches; and,
- applying correct welding procedures (e.g., lap joint or butt joint and spot or plug weld).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine patches to ensure repairs are ready for refinishing and painting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Estimate how much body filler and hardener is needed to repair damaged surfaces.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform appropriate procedures and select appropriate tools to prepare work areas for body filling.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practice proper safety procedures for welding and using cut-off wheels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when repairing contoured panels.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out surface preparation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Surface Preparation (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the range of corrective work procedures for surface preparation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess the damage and research and prepare an estimate of the cost to prepare surfaces for repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify types of material and choose appropriate products and tools following original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify various types of plastic and choose compatible materials and tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform spot repair and surface preparation for metal or plastic surfaces.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop assessment criteria with peers to assess the quality of the repair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the quality of own and peer’s repair to provide feedback on the strengths and areas for improvement.

outcomes.statement: Estimate the damage and time required to carry out repairs on an automobile.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Estimating Repair Costs (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Analyze the role of insurance in the autobody trade in Saskatchewan and elsewhere including:
- describing insurance, liability, waiver, total loss, premium, deductible and package policy;
- examining the role and responsibilities of the insurance adjuster/broker, automobile appraiser, automobile owner(s) and autobody repair shop; and,
- comparing original equipment manufacturer (OEM), recycled, remanufactured and after-market parts to repair an automobile.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Estimate damage repair costs including:
- detailed description of all labour operations that must be performed;
- complete list of parts and materials needed for the repair; and,
- total price including labour, parts, materials and applicable taxes.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Interpret technical service bulletins about potential issues that could result in the need for automobile repairs.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the extent of the damage from outside the automobile and work inward and list everything by section that is bent, broken or missing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the conditions that make an automobile a total loss.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain autobody air, hydraulic and electric tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Advanced Tooling (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 3 and 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the safe use of air, hydraulic and electric tools such as pneumatic chisel, air ratchet, impact wrench, air polisher, air sand blaster, blow gun, air metal shears, power riveter, floor jack, safety stand and hydraulic rams and attachments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform correct procedures when using hand, stationary and power tools for specific autobody repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect air, hydraulic and electric tools before use and tag for repair as required.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain and store air, hydraulic and electric tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize and follow safe work practices when using air, hydraulic and electric tools.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research and estimate the cost to purchase air, hydraulic and electric tools to enter the autobody trade.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas to refinish and repaint parts of an automobile.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Automobile Refinishing and Repainting (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-30 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Estimate technical measurements and determine appropriate procedures and materials to refinish and repaint parts of an automobile.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate of the materials needed to refinish and repaint parts of an automobile.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Practice proper safety techniques when using a sandblaster for metal preparation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply proper sanding techniques using the appropriate type of sand paper to prepare the surface for painting.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the use of reducers and thinners in autobody repair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practice proper techniques and safety procedures to use a spray gun (e.g., siphon and gravity fed), air compressor, air hose and air regulator to paint part or all of an automobile.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Differentiate between the types of spray booths such as a prep station, downdraft, semi-downdraft and cross-draft used in autobody repair.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and method of application of different types (e.g., epoxy primer, urethane primer surface, polyester primer, urethane sealer and acid etch) of automotive primers.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the purpose and method of application of different (e.g., acrylic lacquer, acrylic enamel, polyurethane and base coat/clear coat) types of automotive paints.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Apply proper techniques to mask an automobile and describe over-masking and under-masking.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures such as wearing coveralls, rubber gloves and safety glasses and using an appropriate respirator to apply automotive primers, sealers and paints.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Examine the effects of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on the environment.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Implement a plan to design and organize the workspace to prevent work-related injuries when refinishing and repainting an automobile.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of structural components in each section of the automobile.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of automobile structural design including major changes and characteristics of selected components.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify front (e.g., cowl, shock towers, radiator and supports, fire wall, fenders, hood), centre (e.g., floor pan, pillars, rocker panel, rear shelf, doors, glass, hinges, side impact beam, roof panel, instrument panel, dash) and rear (e.g., trunk floor, trunk lid, quarter panel, lower rear panels, rear shock towers, inner wheel housing, upper body panel) section components of an automobile.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the construction and safety features of plastic bumpers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify part numbers, prices, installation time and procedures using original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications and software and/or manuals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe proper safety procedures used by certified technicians to disable an automobile air bag sensor system.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the properties of dissimilar automotive materials (e.g., carbon, fibre, plastic, stainless).

outcomes.statement: Assess complex metal damage and carry out repairs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Advanced Metal Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-25 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 6, 7 and 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the original point of impact to a panel from a collision to determine potential corrective repairs.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate of the materials used for metal repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper use of hand and power tools to contour metal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify all direct and indirect damage to panels.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Remove glass and trim, if needed, before attempting to straighten metal.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Remove damage from the least damaged area to the worst damaged area.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine the amount of body filler needed to repair damage.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Repair major damage using picking tools, dent pullers, uni-spot pullers, body spoons, suction cups and hydraulic rams.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inspect repair and carry out adjustments as necessary to complete repair.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and follow safe work practices when using hand and power tools.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Implement a plan to design and organize the workspace to prevent work-related injuries related to metal repair.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine the effects of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on the environment.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Investigate and describe short- and long-term health concerns related to body filling products and dust in the workplace.

outcomes.statement: Assess panel misalignment issues and carry out repairs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Panel Alignment (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 3 and 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the range of corrective work procedures that may be required to align a panel.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine panel misalignment issues (e.g., vertical misalignment, loose latches, hinges) that require corrective action.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate to align a panel.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the appropriate corrective action and tools to align a panel (e.g., hood, door, trunk lid, fender, quarter panel).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine proper measurements for panel alignment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper use of hand and power tools to align panels.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize and follow safe work practices when using appropriate hand and power tools to align panels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when conducting panel alignment.

outcomes.statement: Analyze types and functions of automobile glass and carry out glass repairs.
