outcomes.statement: Examine appropriate procedures to ensure food safety in the kitchen.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4A: Food Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the causes of food contamination (e.g., biological, chemical and physical) that can occur in a commercial kitchen.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List examples of biological (e.g., bacteria and viruses), chemical (e.g., cleaners and disinfectants) and physical (e.g., glass or metal fragments) contaminants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify causes of food-borne illnesses (e.g., food poisoning and food allergies).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between direct contamination and cross-contamination.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss common food safety steps (e.g., clean, separate, cook and chill) to reduce food contamination.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate date labelling (e.g., best-before, packaged on and expiration) on pre-packaged foods.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the importance of kitchen sanitation and personal hygiene in the prevention of food contamination and food-borne illnesses.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine safe and sanitary practices to dispose of kitchen waste.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the role of municipal, provincial and national food safety legislation and regulations.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate appropriate food safety standards when receiving, selecting, handling, preparing, serving and storing food.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate appropriate measurement techniques used in commercial cooking.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify measurements (e.g., weight, volume and count) common to the commercial cooking.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe measurements traditionally used in commercial cooking including weight (e.g., As purchased – AP and Edible portion – EP), volume, count, dry and wet measurement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify measurement tools (e.g., measuring spoons, measuring cups, thermometers and kitchen scales) common to a commercial kitchen.

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Convert recipe measurements from imperial to metric (e.g., teaspoon to millilitres and pounds to grams) and metric to imperial.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Measure ingredients using liquid, dry and displacement methods.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper scaling techniques.

indicators.text: Develop criteria to assess the menu.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the importance of menu options for a variety of dietary considerations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6C: Inclusive Menu Options (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 6B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify reasons for including menu options to address personal, cultural or medical dietary preferences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research menus and recipes that include menu options for consumers with dietary preferences.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the legal issues within the food service industry linked to dietary preference (e.g., peanut and shellfish allergies) and related food safety procedures (e.g., cross-contamination and signage on buffets and menus).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the benefits and challenges of offering inclusive menu options.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss establishments (e.g., restaurants, school cafeterias, hospital and long-term care facilities) that would offer menu options to meet the needs of clients and customers.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Design a menu that includes menu options to address dietary preferences, considering factors such as budget and pricing, sustainability and access to local suppliers for ingredients.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Consult resources such as Canada’s Food Guide and Eating Well with Canada’s Food Guide-First Nations, Inuit and Métis to develop menu options.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Select and prepare menu options to address dietary preferences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Create labels for each menu item to specify ingredients for customers and clients.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Calculate the cost of recipes and the selling price of menu options.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Reflect on the prepared menu and document suggestions for improvements.

outcomes.statement: Apply the three methods of heat transfer to cook food.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: Cooking Methods A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define cooking.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate among the three methods (e.g., conduction, convection and radiation) of heat transfer.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare dry heat (e.g., roasting, broiling and sautéing) and moist heat (e.g., simmering, steaming and poaching) cooking methods.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore combination cooking methods (e.g., braising, stewing and sous vide).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain the choice of cooking methods for different recipes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply the cooking method (e.g., dry heat, moist heat and combination) required for a variety of recipes.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Apply kitchen safety and sanitation practices when cooking food.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the effects of cooking methods on food.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7B: Cooking Methods B (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the effects of heat (e.g., change in shape, colour and flavour) on foods such as carbohydrates, fibre, water, proteins and fats.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine the appropriate cooking method to achieve a desired result with a specific ingredient.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize the smoke point and rancidity of various oils and determine the appropriate oil to use for sautéing and deep frying.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the six enemies of fat (i.e., water, soap, salt, breadcrumbs, air and heat).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate dry heat cooking methods that do not involve fat (e.g., roasting, broiling and grilling).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Use dry heat cooking methods that involve fat (e.g., sautéing, pan frying and deep frying).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate moist heat cooking methods such as simmering, steaming and poaching.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate combination cooking methods such as braising, stewing and sous vide.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Analyze the impact (e.g., texture, tenderness and taste) of cooking methods on foods.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Determine the advantages and challenges of using a variety of cooking methods.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Apply kitchen safety and sanitation practices when cooking food.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate effective knife skills.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8A: Knife Skills A (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 5C

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss basic rules of knife safety such as using the correct knife for the task, cutting away from yourself, never leaving a knife in the sink and remaining focused on the task.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss potential injuries (e.g., cuts, strains and sprains) related to knife use.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Classify a variety of knives (e.g., paring, chef’s, serrated, utility and butcher) according to their applications and procedures for use.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the materials of construction (e.g., stainless steel, carbon steel and ceramic) and the parts (e.g., heel, tang and cutting edge) of a knife.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to properly carry a knife (e.g., hold the knife point down, parallel and close to your leg).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply proper techniques to grip and control a knife to produce desired cuts.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the importance of maintaining a sharp knife.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate the process of sharpening and honing a knife.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the purposes for different types of knife cuts such as chopping, dicing, mincing and slicing.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Apply proper cutting techniques (e.g., trimming, peeling, dicing, chopping, julienne, and slicing) for a variety of tasks such as cutting vegetables for a mirepoix or a stir fry.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper cleaning (e.g., wash by hand) and storage of knives.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise the rules of knife safety.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate advanced knife skills and cutting techniques.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8B: Knife Skills B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 8A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe and appropriate use of knives.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research specialty knives such as boning knife, scimitar, channel, ulu, tourne and crooked knife.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Categorize knives according to purpose, including appropriate procedures for use.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective use of specialized knives (e.g., boning knife, scimitar, channel and tourne).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research a variety of advanced knife cuts such as brunoise, chiffonade, parisienne, rondelle and batonnet.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Select the appropriate knife for a particular task.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective advanced knife cuts.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss purposes for using alternative kitchen tools and equipment (e.g., robot coupe, food processor, buffalo chopper, fry cutter and mandoline) to cut food.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Select appropriate cutting tools and equipment (e.g., robot coupe, food processor, buffalo chopper, fry cutter and mandoline) for identified tasks.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Maintain, clean and properly store knives, cutting tools and equipment.

outcomes.statement: Examine the impact of garnishes, decorations and food presentation on hot and cold menu items.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Food Presentation, Garnish and Decoration A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 4B, 8A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify techniques (e.g., use of specific foods and plating) for effective food presentation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the function and characteristic of garnishes.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify garnishes on plated dishes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Critique images of plated foods and identify key elements (e.g., colour, shape, texture and flavour).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine appropriate garnishes for plated dishes based on colour, shape, texture and flavour.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Create garnishes for hot and cold menu items using the fundamentals of plating (e.g., balance, focal point and composition).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise effective plate presentation such as selection of plate size and shape and cleaning the rim of the plate to enhance plate presentation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore how current food trends and social media influence food presentation.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when handling, preparing, serving and storing garnishes and decorations.

outcomes.statement: Create garnishes and decorations for hot and cold buffet items.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9B: Food Presentation, Garnish and Decoration B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-8 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 8B, 9A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between garnishes for buffets and plated dishes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the fundamentals of plating including balance, portion size, visual appeal and arrangement on plates.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the presentation of hot and cold buffet items including platters.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create fruit and vegetable garnishes using proper knife skills (e.g., tourné, spiralize and chiffonade) and garnishing tools (e.g., parisienne scoop, vegetable peeler and zester).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Prepare a buffet using cold food platter presentation considering design and garnishes (e.g., vegetable and fruit roses, carrot curls, celery fans, turnip and onion flowers).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Store garnished fruits and vegetables following appropriate methods (e.g., ice water and wet paper towel).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Prepare garnishes for hot buffet items considering presentation and food safety.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when handling, preparing, serving and storing garnishes and decorations.

outcomes.statement: Examine techniques to prepare, cook and store fruits and vegetables.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10A: Vegetables and Fruits A (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 4A, 7A, 8A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare and classify a variety of fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss factors that affect the storage of fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the common parts (e.g., peel, pith, flesh, seeds and pits) of various fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Provide example of common fruits (e.g., apples, berries, lemons, bananas, and peaches) and vegetables (e.g., beets, cabbage, lettuce, onions, peas and potatoes).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Categorize, using the senses, the flavours and textures of various fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prepare colourful crudité plates using suitable vegetables and proper knife skills (e.g., batonnet, florets and julienne).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Prepare a variety of hot vegetable items using proper knife skills (e.g., julienne, dice and batonnet).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Utilize appropriate cooking methods for hot vegetable items.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess how cooking times and methods affect nutritional values, texture, flavour and colour of fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate food safety standards when handling, preparing, cooking, serving and storing fruits and vegetables.

outcomes.statement: Explore the effects of cooking methods on the texture, flavour, colour and nutritional value of fruits and vegetables.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10B: Vegetables and Fruits B (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 7B, 10A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the effects of a variety of dry heat cooking methods (e.g., roasting, sautéing, caramelizing, grilling) on the texture, colour and flavour of fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the effects of a variety of moist heat cooking methods (e.g., poaching, boiling, blanching, steaming) on texture, colour and flavour to ensure maximum nutrition of fruits and vegetables.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare large and small batch cooking methods for fruits and vegetables, considering factors such as using various methods for a large quantity (e.g., blanching and then deep-frying) and the loss of quality.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Select and prepare vegetables and fruits for menu items based on season and availability.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Assess how cooking times and methods affect the nutritional values, texture, flavour and colour of fruits and vegetable.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prepare fermented foods (e.g., cucumbers, beets, asparagus, cabbage and carrots).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Select and prepare wild fruits or vegetables (e.g., chokecherries, Saskatoon berries, edible flowers and chanterelle mushrooms) using traditional First Nations and Métis cooking methods.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when handling, preparing, cooking, serving and storing fruits and vegetables.

outcomes.statement: Create a variety of salads and dressings.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Salads and Dressings (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 2, 4A, 5A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the four required components (i.e., base, body, garnish and dressing) of a salad.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the main types (e.g., tossed/composed, bound, vegetable, fruit and combination) of salads.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Prepare a variety of salads, including the four required components.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the four categories (e.g., appetizer, accompaniment, main course, and dessert) of salads that can be offered on a menu.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare various salad greens, including lettuces, spinach, spicy greens, bitter greens, cabbages and herbs.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify sources (e.g., farmers’ markets, school greenhouses and local community gardens) of locally sourced produce suitable for salad making.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Differentiate among the four main types of salad dressings (i.e., vinaigrette, emulsified vinaigrette, mayonnaise and mayonnaise-based).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Utilize common ingredients (e.g., vinegars, oils, herbs, spices and mustard) to prepare dressings.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Prepare the four types of salad dressings.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain how to pair dressings for salads.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate knife skills necessary for salad making.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe characteristics of high-quality serving practices.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Demonstrate food safety standards when handling, preparing, serving and storing salads, specifically those containing mayonnaise and raw eggs.

outcomes.statement: Design and prepare a variety of sandwiches, including wraps and pizzas.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Sandwiches (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 10A, 11

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the history of sandwiches.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the different types and styles of sandwiches.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the main components (i.e., bread or bread substitutions, spread and filling) of sandwiches.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Discuss how locally sourced and foraged foods could be incorporated into sandwiches.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Consider preparation and serving practices necessary for dietary needs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Prepare international and specialty sandwiches, considering personal, cultural and medical dietary preferences and needs.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop criteria to assess the prepared sandwiches.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Practise the principles of sanitation and cleaning of the work area.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate food safety standards when preparing, servicing and storing sandwiches, including fillings and toppings.

outcomes.statement: Prepare and present a variety of hors d’oeuvres and appetizers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Appetizers and Hors d’oeuvres (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 3B, 4B, 5A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the difference between hors d’oeuvres, canapés and appetizers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research purpose and variety of hors d’oeuvres.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Collaborate with peers to determine characteristics (e.g., taste, visual appeal and aroma) of high quality hors d’oeuvres.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Plan, prepare and present canapés, relishes and dips (e.g., guacamole, salsa, hummus and tzatziki).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate various methods of serving hors d’oeuvres.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practise appropriate personal hygiene and the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when preparing, serving and storing hors d’oeuvres and appetizers.

outcomes.statement: Produce convenience and scratch stocks.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14: Stocks (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 10A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between convenience and scratch stocks.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify basic stock ingredients.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the list of ingredients in convenience stocks.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss important terminology (e.g., degrease, blanching bones, sachet bag, mirepoix and deglaze) associated with preparing convenience stocks and scratch stocks.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze features (e.g., colour, taste, nutritional value and preparation time) of convenience stocks and scratch stocks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prepare a scratch stock using appropriate cooking methods and processes such as degreasing and skimming.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare cook time, caramelizing and use of acids in different types of stocks such as brown, white, vegetable, fish and specialty stocks (e.g., lamb and ham).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Compare flavours of a soup prepared with convenience stock to a soup made with a scratch stock.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate food safety standards when preparing, cooking, serving and storing stocks and soups.

outcomes.statement: Prepare broth and cream soups using convenience and scratch stocks.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15A: Soups A (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 14

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the types of soups and soup recipes (e.g., tortilla, hot and sour, Three Sisters, borscht, Métis boulette and bisque) from a variety of cultures, including Métis and First Nations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the elements of broth soups and cream soups.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Prepare broth soups using a convenience stock and a scratch stock.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare the colour, texture and flavours of a broth soup made with scratch stock to a broth soup made with a convenience stock.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss steps common to the creation of all cream soups.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prepare a cream soup.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine the ingredients and steps to prepare an industry standard soup.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine soups for proper consistency (e.g., smoothness, richness, thickness, body and ingredient size).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Apply techniques (e.g., flavouring with spices, reduction and thickening) to achieve suitable colour, flavour and texture of soups, and to maintain nutritive values.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate food safety standards when preparing, cooking, serving and storing stocks and soups.

outcomes.statement: Investigate a variety of thickening techniques to prepare soups.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15B: Soups B (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 15A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and types of thickening agents (e.g., slurry, beurre manié, white roux, whitewash and starchy vegetables).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to make a variety of thickening agents.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the use of thickening agents in the preparation of soups (e.g., lentil, vegetable, coconut curry and lemon rice).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a soup using a specific thickening technique.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop criteria to assess the soup and the thickening technique.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the soup, using the developed criteria, and document progress.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when preparing, cooking, serving and storing soups.

outcomes.statement: Create a variety of soups including consommé, specialty and cold soups.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15C: Soups C (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-8 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 15B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research soups, including consommé, specialty and cold soups, from a variety of cultures, including Métis and First Nations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine the purpose and uses of consommé and stock.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Prepare consommé and evaluate for consistency and colour.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Prepare specialty soups such as scotch broth, oxtail, and borscht and, considering factors such as cost, ingredients and cooking techniques.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the two categories of cold soups (i.e., soups that require cooking and soups that do not require cooking).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prepare cold soups (e.g., vichyssoise, gazpacho, strawberry and watermelon) from both categories of cold soups.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Apply preparation and cooking skills appropriate to each soup (e.g., whisking, stock reduction and deglaze), considering factors such as texture, time and heat.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when preparing, cooking, serving and storing soups.

outcomes.statement: Create the five mother sauces and appropriate derivative sauces.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16A: Sauces A (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 7B, 14

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate among the five mother sauces (i.e., béchamel, velouté, espagnole, tomato and hollandaise).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare the five mother sauces (i.e., béchamel, velouté, espagnole, tomato and hollandaise).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the term derivative sauce.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research derivative sauces that can be made from each of the mother sauces.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Select an appropriate mother sauce to create derivative sauces.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore different techniques for incorporating a roux.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the need for matching a specific roux to the appropriate stocks.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Determine which finishing technique (e.g., reducing, straining, deglazing, enriching with butter, cream and seasoning) to use based on the selected sauce.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Apply the skills (e.g., whisking, deglazing, stock reduction, separating eggs) appropriate to each sauce considering factors such as texture, time and heat.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when preparing, cooking, serving and storing sauces.

outcomes.statement: Explore a variety of butter sauces and modern sauces to pair with appropriate menu items.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16B: Sauces B (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 16A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the use of butter sauces and modern sauces to enhance menu items.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a variety of butter sauces (e.g., brown butter, beurre blanc and meuniere butter).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Provide examples and uses of small sauces with menu items.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create small sauces (e.g., cream, mornay, soubise, poulette and creole) to accompany appropriate menu items.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create sauces to enhance the flavour, texture and colour of a menu item (e.g., beurre blanc with white fish and compound butter with grilled food).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the shallow-poaching process with cooking liquid used in the reduction for a beurre blanc sauce.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Prepare a variety of modern sauces (e.g., coulis, relish, cream reduction, chutney, salsa, purée) to pair with appropriate menu items.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Determine whether a sauce is appropriate (e.g., brown sauce served with most red meats as compared to fish or poultry and white sauces for fish dishes as compared to red meats) for the flavour of the food pairing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Practise food safety standards when preparing, cooking, serving and storing sauces.

outcomes.statement: Prepare common breakfast meals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Egg Cookery and Breakfast (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 4A, 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Classify eggs according to grade and size.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the composition of eggs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify correct temperature of coagulation of eggs.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Prepare breakfast meats (e.g., ham, sausage and bacon).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Prepare pancakes, waffles and French toast.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Select and prepare grain cereals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore breakfast dishes from a diversity of cultures, including Métis and First Nations.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify types of fruits and vegetables used in breakfast cookery.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate food safety standards when handling, preparing, cooking, serving and storing eggs.

outcomes.statement: Examine the uses of dairy products and dairy alternatives.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Dairy and Dairy Alternatives (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 4C

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Categorize the major milk, cream and butter products.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate why milk curdles or scorches.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

outcomes.statement: Identify various roles and influences of communication media in school and society.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Communication Through Media (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss and clarify the purposes for communication media including established examples such as video, audio, and interactive media and emerging examples such as blogs, wikis, social networking, and multiple platforms.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and explain a communications model which includes aspects such as the message, the sender, the mode of transmission, the receiver, and any interactivity.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe specific examples where there is emphasis on communication in society (e.g., school, community, home).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Provide some judgement of and justification for effective communications processes and practices (e.g., ads, business, embedded media).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect and articulate personal learning goals for using communication media.

outcomes.statement: Investigate and articulate legal issues related to media such as copyright, privacy, and consent.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: Legal and Ethical Issues (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define the term “copyright” in relation to Canadian law and assess its impact on a Communication Media class.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the three factors that place some works in the public domain and cite some examples of these works along with reasons for their inclusion.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate and report on current issues and resources connected to copyright law such as “open source”, “creative commons”, and stock resources.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate and report on the need for consent in various circumstances such as location, appearance, material, and music.

outcomes.statement: Discuss and reflect on the need for societal standards (e.g., legal, ethical, and community norms, and values) and cultural sensitivity in media.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2B: Legal and Ethical Issues (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Formulate a list of societal standards in relation to issues including sexism, racism, and homophobia and support the list with positive media examples.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compose a strategy for inclusion of appropriate language, content, and images reflective of societal standards in personal, class, and school projects and assignments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and discuss various rating systems for media such as television, movies, and games.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify and discuss some issues regarding posting of images on the web including safety, possible consequences, and permanence of web postings.

outcomes.statement: Identify through research the positive and negative aspects of creative, artistic, and intellectual works receiving ownership protection.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2C: Legal and Ethical Issues (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 2B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Utilize the Canadian Intellectual Property Office to distinguish between copyright, a patent, and an industrial design and identify some common examples.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Collect and categorize a number of articles from various sources regarding intellectual property which reflect opposing points of view.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain and support a personal stance on intellectual property.

outcomes.statement: Investigate and articulate the tasks and skills, including project management, required by various media during the stages of preproduction, production, and postproduction.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create broad definitions of preproduction, production, and postproduction as they pertain to communication media.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare two different media in terms of the work done during preproduction, production, and postproduction.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the key roles in various types of media productions and generate a list of their functions during preproduction.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain project management concepts including timelines, breakdown into smaller tasks, budget, roles, responsibilities, and delivery.

outcomes.statement: Assess the career opportunities in existing and emerging communication media in Saskatchewan, Canada, and globally including post-secondary education and training programs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Career Opportunities (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify specific examples of skills required in Communication Media courses that fall into the categories identified by Human Resources and Skills Development Canada (HRSDC) as Essential Skills and by the Conference Board of Canada (CBofC) as Employability Skills.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the Essential Skills from HRSDC and Employability Skills from the CBofC and correlate them to the skills needed to build a successful career in communication media.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate programming offered by the universities inside and outside of Saskatchewan as well as SIAST and other technical institutes to examine the breadth of post-secondary education programs available in communication media studies including industry association programming such as the Saskatchewan Motion Picture Industry Association and the Saskatchewan Music Association.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Contribute to the collective knowledge of the class through research and sharing on the general activities and opportunities for careers in media production including entrepreneurial aspects.

outcomes.statement: Clearly articulate and demonstrate an understanding of the preproduction process.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Preproduction Processes (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and explain effective strategies to create the production elements during preproduction such as creating the production, determining the intention, identifying the content, predicting the audience effect, creating a treatment, writing a script, and making a storyboard.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify types of hardware and software used in media communications and explain how they are used effectively to produce communications.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Apply critical thinking and decision making regarding the relationship among the production intention, the target audience, and the technology format.

outcomes.statement: Develop and demonstrate increasing skill through the practice and use of equipment (e.g., camera, lights) and processes (e.g., camera work, set lighting) during the typical steps of the production stage of shooting video and beginning postproduction.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify various video formats and explain their current general usage.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and demonstrate industry standard practices of video camera use for positioning (e.g., eye level, high and low angles, point of view), framing (e.g., wide shot, close-up, two shot), movement (e.g., tilt, pan, zoom), and depth of field.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the purposes of lighting in a video and reasons why different lighting would be used (e.g., mood, clarity of images).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate an understanding of motivated lighting effects such as ambient, manipulated, one, two, and three-point lighting.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Understand and explain the challenges for the recording of audio in a single system video production.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate postproduction techniques by editing video shot to complete a simple cut such as an entrance or exit cut.

outcomes.statement: Develop, refine, and appraise personal skills and understandings acquired in Module 6A while experimenting with postproduction activities.

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Critique the composition of some sample videos looking for examples of techniques that add interest to shots such as adding depth, and the rule of thirds.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Frame faces to create interest for the viewer by applying the rule of thirds, using correct headroom and nose room.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Experiment with motivated lighting effects to gain an understanding of how light is used effectively.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss and demonstrate the differences between transitional devices such as dissolves and cuts.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate increasing skill in editing by completing various shot-to-shot transitions such as an entrance cut, an exit cut, and an action cut.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create a personal assessment of acquired skills and understandings to share with the instructor.

indicators.label: d

outcomes.statement: Apply various problem-solving strategies to solve programming problems throughout Computer Science 20.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the computational thinking concepts of decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Provide examples of the importance of computational thinking in many fields (e.g., physics, biology, mathematics, geology, linguistics, psychology and economics).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Generalize a specific solution to a problem to solve multiple problems of similar type (e.g., moving a character in a grid world to the origin regardless of its initial position).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Design algorithms that allow computers and humans to solve problems effectively.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Use flowcharts, pseudocode and/or visual programming environments to model the logic of algorithms.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze and implement programs with the goal of improving code to achieve the most elegant solution.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages of subdividing a problem into smaller components.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze existing code to predict output, and verify the prediction if possible.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the strenghts and limitations of visual programming environments versus text-based languages.

outcomes.statement: Use common coding techniques to enhance code elegance and troubleshoot errors throughout Computer Science 20.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss and implement appropriate coding style (e.g., indentation and comments) and naming conventions for the programming language used in Computer Science 20.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the concept of elegance in coding.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Improve the elegance of existing code by simplifying, improving efficiency and enhancing code readability.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create internal documentation (e.g., inline comments and header comments) for a program.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss different types of errors (e.g., syntax, semantic and runtime) and their impacts on program execution.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify and correct errors in a program.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Use pair programming to write and debug programs, with students experiencing both driver and navigator roles.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop testing procedures, such as outputting values during execution, to debug programs.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Implement exception handling to validate user input.

outcomes.statement: Utilize different data types, including integer, floating point, Boolean and string, to solve programming problems.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between variables and values.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify values of different data types (e.g., integer, floating point, Boolean and string) that can be stored in variables.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Choose and utilize appropriate data types in a program.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the importance of conventions and rules for naming variables within programming languages.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Distinguish between the concepts of assignment and comparison of variables.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Utilize relational operators, including assignment (=), equivalence (==), not equal (!=), greater than (>) and less than (<), in a program.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Write expressions using math operators (e.g., addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), division (/), integer division (//) and modulo division (%))

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Provide examples of problems that require data type conversion.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform data type conversions (e.g., string to integer, floating point to integer and integer to Boolean).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Perform data type conversions (e.g., string to integer, floating point to integer and integer to Boolean

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss the implications of using floating point values, with reference to the concept of precision (e.g., calculations with currenct and rounding errors).

outcomes.statement: Investigate how control structures affect program flow.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the necessity of control structures in programming.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Utilize decistion-making structures (e.g., IF, IF-ELSE and SWITCH) to control the order in which instructions execute.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Utilize WHILE and FOR loops to control program flow and to solve problems with an indefinite or definite number of iterations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine which type of looping structure allows for the most elegant solution to a problem.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Solve problems utilizing nested loops.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the role of logical operators (e.g., AND (&&), OR (||) and NOT(!)) in compound conditional statements.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss operator precedence and how to use parentheses to control the evaluation of Boolean expressions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how to simplify code using control structures and operators.

outcomes.statement: Construct and utilize functions to create reusable pieces of code.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the benefits of using built-in and user-defined functions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Incorporate built-in math functions, including random number generation, in programs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the concepts of local and global scope and the implication of their use, including scalability problems when using global variables.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop user-defined functions that utilize argument passing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the difference between parameters (variables) and arguments (values) in functions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Incorporate built-in string functions such as length, substring and concatenation in programs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how functions enable programmers to reuse code easily in multiple situations.

outcomes.statement: Investigate one-dimensional arrays and their applications.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Provide examples of the types of problems that can be solved using arrays.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the advantages of using one-dimensional arrays to manipulate multiple values using loops.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe errors, such as out of bounds errors, which can occur when using arrays.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Write a program that creates, accesses and modifies a one-dimensional array.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate and use built-in array functions (e.g., length and sort) included within a programming language.

outcomes.statement: Explore the underlying technology of computing devices and the internet, and their impacts on society.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate how computing devices function and how the Internet allows connected devices to communicate.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the history of computing devices and the Internet, including key milestones and contributors.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the units used to measure computing specifications such as data storage capacity, processing speed and transmission speed.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the role of typical hardware (e.g., CPU, wireless card, RAM, graphics card, SIM card, hard drive and motherboard) found within computing devices.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the role of technologies (e.g., packets and routing) and protocols (e.g., DNS, IP addresses, HTTP and FTP) that support information transfer on the Internet

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the societal impacts of ubiquitous Internet access, cloud computing and connected devices.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore implications of advances in computing performance.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss limitations of current technologies and predict possible directions of future technologies.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore the interactions between humans and computing devices.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the impacts of information technologies on privacy, including digital security practices.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe legal and ethical issues related to the use of computing devices (e.g., social media, advertising, encryption, malicious software and social engineering).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore how issues related to personal rights and privacy such as identity theft, data collection, permanence of information on the Internet and surveillance are affected by technologies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the role of different layers (e.g., network, operating system, application and data) of digital security, including the responsibility of users.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits and limitations of user authentication techniques to prevent or allow access to resources

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research data encryption techniques used for storage and transmission.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the role of personal responsibility in the context of access and use of confidential information, including intellectual property rights and plagiarism.

outcomes.statement: Explore computer science related career paths in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research and describe career choices and trends in computer science in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research which programming languages are prominent in specific computer science sub-fields such as game, website and mobile development.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and report on opportunities for experiential learning (e.g., co-op programs, job shadowing and career fairs) in the field of computer science.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inquire into issues of gender equity and diversity of the computer science workplace, considering questions such as "Why are females and certain cultural groups typically underrepresented in the computer science workplace in Saskatchewan?" and "What steps could be take to encourage more females to pursue computer science related careers?"

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research and report on postsecondary educational programs leading to careers in information systems and computer science (e.g., institutions offering relevant programs, industry certifications, courses of study, entrance requirements, length of programs and costs).

indicators.label: f

outcomes.statement: Develop a coding project and/or research a topic related to computer science of the student's choice.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a proposal document for a coding project that includes discussion of the basic premise or problem to be solved, key features and project team members and their roles.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Construct a tool (e.g., rubric, checklist, self-evaluation form or peer-evaluation form) to assess the process and products involved in a student-directed study.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Develop a coding project using the same or a different programming language than those used in Computer Science 20.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine an area of collaborative research between computer science and another field.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the application of computer science in other fields (e.g., art, trades, sciences, mathematics and medicine).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inquire into the current state and/or societal implications of a current trend in computing such as hacking, artificial intelligence, robotics, microcontrollers, game design, cryptography, mobile development or intellectual property.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Present the research or project to peers.

indicators.text: Access search engines, forums and question and answer sites independently to find solutions to coding problems.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore collaborative programming practices and models.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Collaborative programming practices and models.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Collaborate with others to plan a solution to a problem.

indicators.label: d

indicators.text: Reflect on the advantages and challenges encountered when working collaborative contexts to solve programming problems.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Interact with experts who work collaborative programming environments.

outcomes.statement: Investigate types of data structures and the advantages of organizing data in different ways.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Provide examples of the types of problems that can be solved using two-dimensional arrays, mutable (dynamic) arrays and associative arrays (e.g., hash tables or dictionaries).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Develop a program the utilizes a two-dimensional array.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Solve a problem utilizing a mutable array (e.g., list or ArrayList).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the use of associative arrays (e.g., hash tables or dictionaries) to store a dataset.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages of using different data structures to solve problems.

outcomes.statement: Create programs that utilize external files.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the types of problems (e.g., high score list, cookie, preferences or output file) that can be solved by utilizing external data.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Load content from a local or remote file into a program.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Parse the data from an external file to remove extraneous information, if necessary.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Save the state of a program by creating or modifying a file.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of saving data into and external file.

outcomes.statement: Use libraries to simplify solutions to programming problems.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the advantages of using libraries (packages) in programs.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a program that imports a package or classes wthin a package.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the functionality of a library from the documentation or application programming interface (API)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Write a program that utilizes an application programming interface (API)(e.g., social networking, weather data, user authentication, photo sharing and geolocation data)

outcomes.statement: Explore the concepts and principles of object-oriented programming.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate object-oriented programing concepts including classes, objects, attributes and methods.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how a class can be understood as a programmer-defined data type.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Design and implement a class, and create a program that utilizes instances of this class.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply the principle of encapsulation through the creation and use of user-defined objects.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create a constructor and use it to instantiate an object.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare object-oriented and procedural programming paradigms.

outcomes.statement: Explore recursion and investigate sorting algorithms.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Distinguish between iterative and recursive problem-solving techniques and demonstrate how to accomplish a specific task using both approaches.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create recursive functions and use them in programs to solve problems such as calculating factorials, evaluating exponents, designing fractal images or calculating the Fibonacci sequence.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the processes (e.g., the stack, stack frames and maximum recursion depth) involved in evaluating recursive functions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identity the advantages and disadvantages of using recursive problems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Provide examples of situations where sorting is used to solve problems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of efficiency in sorting algorithms.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze the execution of insertion, selection and quicksort algorithms using visualizations.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Illustrate the implementation of a sorting algorithm (e.g., selection, insertion, and quicksort) using pseudocode.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Create a program to sort data in an array using one or more sorting algorithms (e.g., selection, insertion, quicksort).

indicators.text: Discuss how all digital data is stored numerically and how the data type dictates the interpretation of the number.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the rationale for using various number systems.

indicators.label: c

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how colour values are represented digitally, including RGB and hexadecimal.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how character encoding systems such as ASCII and Unicode represent text.

outcomes.printedWith: Module 1A: Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss worker and employee rights and responsibilities as they relate to workplace safety and how they can prevent injuries.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common safety hazard categories and hierarchy of control common to the construction industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate the risks (e.g., slips, trips, falls) and potential safety hazards in the jobsite and shop workspace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the benefits of completing the different certifications and programs offered by Work Safe Sask, Sask Safety Council, Sask Prevention and the Ministry of Labour Relations and Workplace Safety.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore basic safety procedures (e.g., storage and maintenance of tools, clean workspace and caution when working at high heights and power tools) as they apply to the jobsite and shop workspace.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a list of rules for workplace safety including proper personal protective equipment (PPE), sanitation, neat and tidy work area and reporting workplace accidents and safety incidents.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Act consistently to focus on personal tasks while maintaining consciousness of others working in proximity.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate the utilization and maintenance of protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform proper lockout and de-energizing of equipment before beginning inspections or repairs.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify the advantages and disadvantages of using each category of industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) for respiratory, hearing, sight and body protection such as masks, ear plugs, safety goggles and shields.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Demonstrate the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station, shower, first aid station, shop ventilation, fire extinguishers and caging devices) in the workplace.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Post and maintain emergency phone numbers in a visible location.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in the event of an injury in the workplace, including whom to contact, how to report and first-aid procedures.

indicators.text: Identify common safety hazard categories and hierarchy of control common to the construction industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate the risks (e.g., slips, trips, falls) and potential safety hazards in the jobsite and shop workspace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the benefits of completing the different certifications and programs offered by Work Safe Sask, Sask Safety Council, Sask Prevention and the Ministry of Labour Relations and Workplace Safety.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore basic safety procedures (e.g., storage and maintenance of tools, clean workspace and caution when working at high heights and power tools) as they apply to the jobsite and shop workspace.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a list of rules for workplace safety including proper personal protective equipment (PPE), sanitation, neat and tidy work area and reporting workplace accidents and safety incidents.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Act consistently to focus on personal tasks while maintaining consciousness of others working in proximity.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate the utilization and maintenance of protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform proper lockout and de-energizing of equipment before beginning inspections or repairs.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify the advantages and disadvantages of using each category of industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) for respiratory, hearing, sight and body protection such as masks, ear plugs, safety goggles and shields.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Demonstrate the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station, shower, first aid station, shop ventilation, fire extinguishers and caging devices) in the workplace.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Post and maintain emergency phone numbers in a visible location.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in the event of an injury in the workplace, including whom to contact, how to report and first-aid procedures.

outcomes.statement: Apply safety standards to prevent injuries in the construction and carpentry workspace.
