indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the various types of formulas, the water to formula ratio and appropriate bottle heating methods.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate burping positions and techniques.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize signs of painful gas, colic and reflux and demonstrate holds and strategies to alleviate them.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research safe sleep practices for infants and infant sleep cycles.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss ways to deal with a crying infant safely (e.g., try to calm the baby, give the baby to a colleague, leave the baby in a safe place for a few minutes, never shake a baby).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective swaddling techniques.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper diapering techniques.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the use of cloth and disposable diaper in early learning and child care environments.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore family and cultural differences in infant care practices.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explore ways to foster positive attachments and relationships with infants.

outcomes.statement: Investigate careers in early learning and child care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Careers in Early Learning and Child Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore various types of professions with a focus on early learning and child care (e.g., early childhood educator, pre-kindergarten and kindergarten teacher, educational assistants, program director, policy advisor).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize the characteristics of an effective early learning and child care caregiver (e.g., compassionate, patient, responsible, attentive).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the expanded roles and responsibilities of a certified early childhood educator (e.g., guide, researcher, observer, documenter).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore various secondary and post-secondary pathways leading to employment involving infants and young children (e.g., dual credit options with high school and post-secondary institutions, collegial certification, university degrees).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine opportunities for volunteering in early learning and child care environments (e.g., obtaining a credit through the Saskatchewan Ministry of Education’s Volunteerism Policy, 2023).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate official certification levels (i.e., levels 1, 2, 3) to become a certified early childhood educator in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate potential earnings of various types of early learning and child care positions in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine inclusive hiring policies and practices in early learning and child care environments (e.g., representation of urban and rural workers, newcomers to Canada, men and gender diverse individuals).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate challenges related to working as an early learning and child care caregiver (e.g., fatigue, stress, mental health).

outcomes.statement: Differentiate between types of early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14: Types of Early Learning and Child Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 13

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Investigate how family needs might differ in urban, suburban, rural and remote communities.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare aspects of regulated family child care homes to those of unregulated family child care homes in Saskatchewan (e.g., subsidy options, parent fees, regulations, training, programs).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare aspects of regulated early learning child care centres to those of regulated family child care homes and unregulated day homes in Saskatchewan (e.g., size, staffing requirements, parent fees, regulations, training, programs).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the cultural mandates (e.g., Indigenous child care theory and practices, promotion of language and culture, choice of materials, relationship with the community) in early learning child care centres.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the requirements for running a regulated family child care home in Saskatchewan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Regulated Family Child Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the three types of family child care homes in Saskatchewan: family child care homes, group family child care homes and teen student support family child care homes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the standards set by the Government of Saskatchewan for running a regulated family child care home (e.g., number of children allowed, age combinations, fire, health and safety requirements).

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Research community organizations (e.g., Saskatchewan Early Childhood Association, l’Association des parents Fransaskois, Healthy Start) that provide information regarding requirements for running a regulated family child care home in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate potential earnings of a regulated family child care home in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the Canada Revenue Agency website for taxation information related to working in the home.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare the requirements of running a regulated family child care home to those of running an unregulated family child care home in Saskatchewan.

outcomes.statement: Examine ways to prevent injuries and promote safety of children.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Safety and Injury Prevention for Children (Core for Early Learning Pathway) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify main causes of early childhood deaths and injury.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate household consumer products that present an injury risk to children (e.g., telephones, soaps and detergents, chairs, light bulbs, dangling blind cords).

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Recognize foods that are dangerous for infants and toddlers (e.g., raw honey, unpasteurized milk, hot dogs, whole grapes).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify choking, strangulation and suffocation hazards (e.g., foods, toys, strings, cords, pillows) and strategies to use to mitigate risk.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research how worldview may impact childrearing practices in terms of safety (e.g., risky play, choice of toys, child guidance).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the difference between the concepts of “as safe as necessary” and “as safe as possible”.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Outline procedures for treating various injuries (e.g., cuts, bites, burns, sunburns, stings).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss ways to prevent accidents and injuries in children at different ages.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research ways to childproof a home for injury prevention.

outcomes.statement: Examine the legal responsibilities and procedures to ensure safety in early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Safety in Early Learning and Child Care Environments (Core for Early Learning Focus) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 16

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the legal expectations for ensuring physically safe environments for children in early learning and child care environments (e.g., adult-child ratios, fire-safety regulations, food-safety regulations, emergency weather preparedness plans, WHMIS regulations).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the purpose of minor incident and major incident reports.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine factors that can lead to neglect or physical, sexual or emotional abuse of children (e.g., family history of violence, stress, addictions).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify possible indicators of child abuse.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the early learning and child care caregiver’s legal responsibility in reporting suspected abuse (e.g., consult the Saskatchewan Child Abuse Protocol 2014).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss privacy laws that protect children’s records.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the procedures related to administering medication (e.g., allergy medication, pain medication, insulin, antibiotics, inhalers) in an early learning and child care environment.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine how early learning and child care environments can respect the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the roles of society in ensuring the safety of children (e.g., Amber Alerts).

outcomes.statement: Examine the roles and responsibilities of a childminder.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Childminding (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 8 and 16

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List the responsibilities of a childminder.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the use of personal devices (e.g., phones) when caring for children.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how to recognize signs of child abuse and neglect and discuss the childminder’s responsibility to report them.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss how to ensure personal safety and security when caring for children in their homes.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify organizations offering First Aid and CPR courses and discuss the benefits of such courses.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore family expectations of childminders when caring for their children (e.g., punctuality, meal preparation, homework, use of personal devices, giving baths).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify different ways of communicating with parents and guardians (e.g., texting, phoning, emailing).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Plan safe and engaging activities for different age groups (e.g., organizing and leading activities for infants, toddlers, preschoolers and school aged children).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss strategies for minding children with exceptionalities (e.g., addressing safety concerns, adaptations).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to talk about hourly pay and payment methods with parents and guardians.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research employment opportunities in the community and abroad as a nanny, au pair or early learning and child care caregiver.

outcomes.statement: Examine how diseases and infections are managed in early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Diseases and Infections in Early Learning and Child Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe positive environmental factors (e.g., good nutrition and dietary habits, daily physical activity, regular medical and dental care, clean and safe home environment) that influence good health in children.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate common communicable diseases (e.g., chicken pox, ringworm, pertussis) in early learning and child care environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore immunizations available in Saskatchewan to protect children at various ages.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore common special health concerns (e.g., allergies, diabetes, epilepsy, asthma) present in early learning and child care environments.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: List steps for controlling the spread of airborne and foodborne illnesses (e.g., hand washing, cough etiquette, sanitizing and disinfecting).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how to care for children who become ill while in early learning and child care environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how illness should be reported to parents and guardians.

outcomes.statement: Explore how nutrition contributes to children’s health in early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: Nutrition for Children (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research nutritional information in Canada’s Food Guide for children up to age six.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the beneficial effects of healthy eating patterns on the growth and development of children from birth to six years of age (e.g., increased ability to concentrate, fewer common childhood illnesses, improved overall health).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the benefits and drawbacks of various infant nutrition (e.g. breastmilk, commercial formula).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss ways to support breastfeeding mothers in early learning and child care environments (e.g., offering private feeding areas, accepting and storing frozen breastmilk).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore diets of various cultures or religions (e.g., Halal, Kosher).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research various cultural practices during mealtimes (e.g., sitting on the floor, eating with one’s hands, being fed by others, not wasting food, silence during meals).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate ways to help children with food preferences (e.g., offering appropriate serving sizes, involving children in the meal preparation, serving foods that reflect cultural and religious backgrounds).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research common food allergies (e.g., nuts, dairy products).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify nutritious substitutions that could be used in a meal plan for children with specific dietary requirements (e.g., Celiac, lactose intolerance, vegetarian diet).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Study meal planning guides and meal planning budgets for early learning and child care environments.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Plan a one-week menu for an early learning or child care environment that take into account costs and food restrictions (e.g., allergies, cultural diets of the local community).

outcomes.statement: Explore child guidance strategies to promote age-appropriate behaviour.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21: Child Guidance (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify situations that cause behavioural challenges (e.g., overstimulation, break in routine, noise, waiting time, frustration, stress) and proposed possible solutions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the efficacy of verbal and non-verbal guidance strategies (e.g., proximity, distraction, redirection).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between direct guidance (i.e., verbal and non-verbal actions) and indirect guidance (i.e., outside factors that influence behaviour such as the physical environment or routine).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective use of praise and encouragement.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss ways to use common child guidance approaches in culturally appropriate ways (e.g., do not expect eye contact form children for whom it is not culturally appropriate).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how to use natural consequences and logical consequences to guide behaviour.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how to offer appropriate choices.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate strategies to assist children with regulating their emotions (e.g., naming feelings, showing empathy).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore time-ins and their alternatives (e.g., special time).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the value of following through and being consistent.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate child guidance strategies based on age groupings (i.e., infants, toddlers, preschoolers, school-aged children).

outcomes.statement: Create a plan for a daily routine in an early learning and child care environment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22: Daily Routines (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of a daily schedule for children.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify which parts of a daily schedule are fixed (e.g., gym time, home time) and which parts of the day may be extended or shortened (e.g., snack time, outdoor play, unstructured play).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the benefits of unstructured play in a daily routine.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the benefits of having a flexible routine (e.g., transitioning to another activity at a natural point).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how to keep transitions and interruptions to children’s activities to a minimum.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate various types of transition tools such as visual cues, rhymes, music and gestures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss ways to communicate routines with parents and caregivers.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify challenging moments of a routine (e.g., dressing, undressing, meals, nap time) and strategies to address them.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate how professionals in early learning and childcare environments support families with potty training routines.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the sleeping routines of infants, toddlers and preschoolers in an early learning and child care environment.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Create a visual schedule of the daily routine including transitions and time for unstructured play.

outcomes.statement: Analyze indoor early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23: Indoor Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify elements of an optimal indoor early childhood learning environment (e.g., open areas for music and movement, quiet spaces, carefully placed culturally responsive materials).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Observe the differences between infant, toddler and preschooler indoor environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the macro level configuration (i.e., overall environment) of an early childhood learning environment (e.g., the location of furniture, accessibility, pathways and flooring and windows).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the micro level set-up (i.e., specific materials found within the space) for an early childhood learning environment (e.g., accessibility, quantities and the cultural and linguistic relevance of materials).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare indoor play spaces organized according to play schemas and centres.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore ways to ensure safety and accessibility in indoor early learning environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how to set up a room to encourage positive interactions and behaviours.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore ways to make an early learning indoor environment visually appealing, comfortable, homelike and culturally relevant.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss ways to use technology (e.g. shows, interactive screens) effectively and responsibly in early learning environments.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss strategies to adapt the environment for children with diverse abilities, temperaments or interests (e.g., quiet spaces, muted color palates, natural light, natural materials).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Design, sketch or create a representation of a floor plan of an indoor early childhood setting.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Research the costs of materials used in early learning and child care environments.

outcomes.statement: Analyze outdoor early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24: Outdoor Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 23

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore a variety of playground design philosophies (e.g., open ended, risky play, inclusive, nature inspired, fitness focused).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship between outdoor education and land-based education.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify elements of an optimal outdoor early childhood learning environment (e. g., plants and flowers native to Saskatchewan to attract insects and birds, equipment to support large muscle development, sheltered areas for protection from the sun and the rain).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify materials that support and extend children’s learning outdoors (e.g., magnifying glasses, identification books, bug keepers, shovels, rakes, water).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify outdoor elements that could be brought indoors (e.g., growing seeds inside, watching bugs in bug keepers, collecting pine cones for an art project).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss strategies to adapt early learning outdoor environments for the safety of children with diverse abilities, temperaments or interests (e.g., uncluttered outdoor setting, modifying hands-on activities, accessible play structures).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss ways to ensure safety when in outdoor environments (e.g., close supervision around water, sun protection measures, cold weather clothing).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the benefits of gardening with children (e.g., providing sensory experiences, engaging families, developing a deeper understanding of where food comes from).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify opportunities and challenges of playing outdoors in all seasons.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Design, sketch or create a representation of an early childhood outdoor environment.

outcomes.statement: Investigate how to support children’s mental health and development of positive sense of self in early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25: Supporting Children’s Mental Health (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore self-concepts (e.g., traits, characteristics, beliefs, behaviours, attitudes) and self-esteem (e.g., how one evaluates aspects of the self).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the characteristics of an environment that promotes good mental health and self-esteem (e.g., safe place to express emotions, positive staff interactions, greetings, children feeling valued, positive relationships with the children and families).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the differences in infant temperaments (e.g., easy-going, slow to warm up, active) and their continuation later in childhood.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify ways to recognize, interpret and respond to a child’s cues.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate strategies to alleviate stress and anxiety in children (e.g., breathing exercises, art therapy, sensory experiences, spending time outdoors, laughter, roughhousing).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate empathy in role-play.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate acknowledging and labeling young children’s feelings.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the benefits of contact with nature on children’s mental health.

outcomes.statement: Explore theories and risk factors related to early childhood mental health.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26: Mental Health Theories and Risk Factors for Children (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 25

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore brain development from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate key developmental theories related to infant and early mental health, such as attachment, resilience and emotional regulation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Research how children’s mental health and development outcomes are impacted by the following factors:
- child factors (e.g., pre-and postnatal experiences and circumstances, temperament);
- socio-demographic and societal factors (e.g., community, environment, level of income); and,
- parental or caregiver factors (e.g., consistency, parenting attitudes and styles).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how to promote secure attachment relationships in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research trauma-sensitive care practices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize potential causes of stress and anxiety for young children (e.g., moving, separation, residual trauma).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Distinguish the three levels of stress (i.e., positive, tolerable, toxic) and their impact on child development.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the impact of stress on brain development, including prenatal and postpartum experiences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Determine early indicators (e.g., withdrawal behaviour, compulsive activities, loss of earlier developmental achievements) of mental health disorders in young children.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify local organizations that support mental health for young children and their families (e.g., Saskatchewan Prevention Institute).

outcomes.statement: Describe how early learning and child care caregivers can develop positive relationships with families and the community.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27: Relationships With Children’s Families (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the benefits of strong collaborative partnerships between early learning and child care caregivers and childrens’ families.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify barriers to positive relations between early learning and child care caregivers and childrens’ families.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss ways to include families in planning activities, supports and resources when appropriate.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe strategies that can improve relationships and communications between caregivers and children’s families (e.g., communication apps, daily verbal reports).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how parents, guardians and families are the experts on their child.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify ways to recognize, respect and incorporate family strengths (e.g., highlighting what is strong rather that what is wrong, confirming things they know they are doing well) when interacting with families.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare a variety of community resources for families with young children.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research facilities (e.g., libraries, family resource centres, community centres) and events (e.g., festivals, theatre, dance, music, sport) that build relationships in the community.

outcomes.statement: Determine ways to support children’s culture, identity and sense of belonging.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28: Children’s Culture and Identity (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss what it means to belong to a family and a community (e.g., birthplace, name, parents, grandparents and community connections).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize how connection to others, place and language influence identity development.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate ways to ensure parents, guardians and families feel included and have a sense of belonging in early learning environments.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate ways to include families’ cultural identities in early learning and child care environments (e.g., books, posters, family pictures, orally transmitted stories, decorations, music).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research ways in which early learning and child care environments can support language learning (e.g., through music, literacy, vocabulary building activities).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify ways to support and foster identity when working with young children (e.g., selecting multilingual books and software, selecting music of various genres that reflect the local contemporary cultural community, using manipulatives and loose parts familiar to the children, learning key words in children’s home language).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe strategies that can be used in early learning and child care environments to challenge gender stereotypes.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research local events of social, ceremonial and community activities available to families with young children.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate protocols for inviting grandparents, family members, Knowledge Keepers or Elders into an early learning setting to share stories, songs, dances or cultural foods.

outcomes.statement: Explore Indigenous approaches to child rearing, nurturing and learning.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29: Indigenous Approaches to Child Rearing (Core for Early Learning Pathway) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research traditional Indigenous prenatal supports, delivery and postpartum care programs available in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Engage with a local First Nations or Métis Elder to talk about traditional early child development teachings.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore cultural teachings related to birth and infancy.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the role of grandparents and Elders in raising children (e.g., transmitting language, ceremony and culture, teaching stories, role modeling).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate kinship relationships and roles of family and community members (e.g., aunties, uncles, stepparents, parents-in-law, existing natural supports) in caring for Indigenous children.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the importance of ancestral language development in traditional approaches to child rearing, nurturing, and learning.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of spending time on the land with young children to support the development of their identity.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the importance of pregnancy, children and older persons in Indigenous communities.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research tipi teachings and how they are applicable to nurturing and development.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify local agencies that can support learning about traditional Indigenous teachings.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research the impact of residential schools, the Sixties Scoop and the millennial scoop on the physical, mental, emotional and spiritual connections between children, parents, families and communities.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the principles of learning through play and exploration.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 30: Play and Exploration (Optional) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Determine the functions of play (e.g., express personal thoughts and feelings, develop self-control, assess risks, develop language and literacy skills).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate Parten’s levels of play (i.e., uninvolved, onlooker, solitary, parallel, associative, cooperative) and the risks of social play.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Observe examples of atypical play to determine the need for further intervention.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the role of play in brain development.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the role of adults as part of the play process (e.g., modeling oral language and emergent literacy, providing props and resources to enrich play, observing children’s play to assess social and cognitive growth).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how adults support safe play (e.g., interrupt and intervene when necessary, watch for safety, differentiate between a risk and a hazard during roughhousing).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare guided play (e.g., when adults participate in play) and free play (e.g., when children engage in self-directed play).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the different types of play schemas (e.g., connection, transformation, trajectory, rotation, envelopment).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Categorize age-appropriate loose parts according to the different types of play schemas (e.g., tape for connecting, spray bottles for transforming, fabrics for enveloping).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Evaluate toys intended for infants, toddlers and preschoolers according to specific criteria such as safety and developmental appropriateness.

outcomes.statement: Explore the physical domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31: Physical Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Distinguish the differences between gross motor skills (e.g., laterality, spatial awareness, left/right dominance, balance) and fine motor skills (e.g., handedness, coordination, dexterity) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the benefits of physical activity for young children (e.g., develops strength, flexibility and endurance, maintain healthy weight, lowers stress and anxiety).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Plan experiences that allow children to develop fine motor skills and represent their learning (e.g., manipulating small objects) for different age groupings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss indoor structures, spaces and equipment (e.g., climbing structures, space to dance, balls, scarves) that promote large muscle development for different age groupings.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create a safe obstacle course or balance trail for different age groupings in which toddlers and preschoolers use loco motor skills such as walking, running, skipping, rolling or maintaining balance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Design an activity or game for different age groupings designed to develop manipulative skills such as throwing, tossing, kicking, catching or striking.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Design an activity or game for different age groupings designed to develop an awareness of space by adjusting their movements around furniture, objects, hazards, adults and children in a common space.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate strategies to develop healthy habits independently (e.g., wearing a bicycle helmet) when engaging in free play.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe the physical developmental skills of a child in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss how children’s physical development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore the social-emotional domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 32: Social-Emotional Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 31

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore aspects related to the social-emotional domain of development (e.g. developing self-concept and self-esteem, regulating emotions, interacting with others) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore self-awareness including name, favourite personal traits, interests, favourite food, extra-curricular activities, community and cultural connections.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research culturally appropriate ways to provide support to children who have difficulty separating from family.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Role play a scene in which an early learning and child care caregiver models strategies to identify and regulate emotions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Model strategies, for different age groupings, to consider the perspective of others and show empathy.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe the social and emotional growth of a child in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how social-emotional development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore the intellectual domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 33: Intellectual Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 32

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore aspects of the intellectual domain of development (e.g., creating and imagining, recognizing attributes and characteristics, exploring numeracy, language and literacy) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research creative representations, constructions or props to encourage imaginative play for toddlers and preschoolers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Curate a selection of open-ended age-appropriate materials, including culturally relevant materials, (e.g., loose parts such as shells, pine cones, small stones, fabrics, wood materials, beads, water containers, clay, tools and utensils) that children can use to recognize attributes and characteristics.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify a selection of age-appropriate tools and devices (e.g., measuring tapes, measuring cups, rulers, sticks) children can use for measurement.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the presence of numeracy in everyday life in an early learning setting (e.g., counting songs, estimating amounts, measuring lengths).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify age-appropriate activities to explore the concept of time (e.g., posting a calendar, talking about seasons, planning long-term multi-step projects).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Create age-appropriate activities to explore positioning (e.g. before, after, over, under, in front, behind).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe the intellectual developmental skills of a child in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss how intellectual development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore the spiritual domain of development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 34: Spiritual Domain of Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 33

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe a memory of sensory perceptions related to the beauty and wonder of the world experienced as a young child.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine what captures the attention, engages the senses and triggers possible emotions after walking or spending time outside.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss ways to safely expose infants, toddlers and preschoolers to the natural world.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate opportunities to explore the senses using natural and culturally relevant materials such as interesting textures to touch (e.g., feathers, pebbles, sticks), smell (e.g. spices, plants, herbs), see (e.g. coloured beads, flowers, birds, mirrors) and hear (e.g. music, wind chimes, instruments).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Brainstorm vocabulary to describe textures, sounds, smells, colours or tastes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how spiritual development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore language and literacy development of infants, toddlers and preschoolers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 35: Language and Literacy Development (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 34

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore aspects related to language and literacy development (e.g., engaging in conversation, exploring words, representing ideas) from birth to six years of age.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how language can be developed through interactions in play.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify opportunities for children to listen with engagement (e.g., musical performances, puppet shows, stories, visits from Elders and grandparents).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate age-appropriate strategies to introduce new vocabulary in an early childhood setting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate asking complex questions (e.g., “How does that work?”, “Why do leaves change colors?”) rather than simple questions (e.g., “What’s that?” or “Where are we going?”).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research songs, poems and books with texts that rhyme, use alliterations and explore different sounds.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate interactive reading with individuals or small groups (e.g., reading with expression, articulating clearly, inviting comments, asking for predictions, sharing feelings and experiences).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze representations of ideas created by children (e.g., drawing, painting, collage, construction, dramatic play).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research the benefits of bilingualism or multilingualism in early childhood.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate how young children learn additional languages (e.g., extended time period to acquire the additional language and build confidence, exploration and play with peers and adults, singing familiar and repetitive songs).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss ways to support the use and development of home language.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Curate a selection of language and literacy materials (e.g., songs, rhymes, books) that are connected to cultures, home languages and familial understandings in the community.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Develop a template to observe children’s language and literacy skills related to the intellectual developmental domain.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss how language and literacy development might influence other areas of development.

outcomes.statement: Explore observation, documentation and assessment processes in early learning and child care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 36: Observation, Documentation and Assessment (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between observation, documentation and assessment.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Investigate developmentally appropriate and culturally responsive assessment practices, such as developing a relationship with the child, administering assessment tools in the child’s first language and allowing children to represent their ideas in a variety of ways.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between screening tools (e.g., observation templates, journals, data collection, notes) and assessment tools (e.g. early years assessments).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore specialized assessments completed by professional specialists (e.g., speech language pathologist, occupational therapist, educational psychologist).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate documentation tools (e.g., pictures, videos, products) used to record the four domains of development.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate appropriate ways (e.g., terminology) to discuss children’s learning and development amongst colleagues or with parents and guardians.

outcomes.statement: Investigate characteristics of an inclusive early learning program.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 37: Inclusive Early Learning Programs (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 36

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare a medical model of supporting children with diverse abilities (i.e., focus on diagnosis) to a holistic needs-based model (i.e., focus on strengths, abilities and needs of the child).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe strategies for responsive teaching such as making evidence-based decisions, valuing relationships and meeting students’ needs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe exceptionalities that may require intensive supports (e.g., visual impairment, deafness, autism spectrum disorder).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate adaptations (e.g., in learning centres or invitations for learning, daily activities and routines) for children needing targeted and intensive supports.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss adaptations (e.g., in learning centres or invitations for learning, daily activities and routines) for children needing universal supports.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the role of the early learning and child care caregiver in documenting and reporting for early intervention (e.g., observe, screen and monitor child development).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss how to collaborate with other professionals and families to develop a holistic understanding of the child.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate how to conduct strengths-based interventions (e.g., acknowledging skills, knowledge, talents, character traits, relationships and abilities rather than deficits).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of talking circles when planning an intervention.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research specialized professions related to early childhood development (e.g., occupational therapist, speech therapist, child psychologist, behaviour therapist, physiotherapist).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Evaluate an indoor and an outdoor environment for children with diverse abilities.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Research local and provincial organizations that offer specialized supports (e.g., Inclusion Saskatchewan, Autism Support Services, Saskatchewan Alternate Format Materials Library, Early Childhood Intervention Program, Kids First, Saskatchewan Prevention Institute).

outcomes.statement: Create an invitation for learning.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 38: Invitations for Learning (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 17, 22, 28, 30 and 36

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define invitations for learning (i.e., a collection of interesting and carefully combined materials that may be used in a number of ways to draw children’s attention).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare thematic planning to child-guided planning.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss preferred ways to present invitations (e.g., visually appealing presentation, materials that define the space, intentional positioning of the objects).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore considerations for designing invitations (e.g., the textures, smells, sounds, materials that change when manipulated or combined, the amount of materials for the number of children, cultural relevancy).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Observe children engaging with an invitation to determine ways to extend learning and play.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine invitations that promote literacy and language development.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore materials that could be used in outdoor invitations (e.g., hub caps, hay bales, steering wheels, pieces of wood).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate ways invitations could be used to support the cultures of children in the program.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore how play schemas and their corresponding loose parts can be incorporated into invitations.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Plan an invitation for learning, including the budget for materials.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Create an invitation for learning for a targeted age grouping (e.g., toddlers, preschoolers).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Evaluate the efficacy of the invitation for learning.

outcomes.statement: Examine supportive care provider careers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 39: Supportive Care Provider Careers (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Describe reasons to work in the health care industry (e.g., personal goals, personal calling, financial goals, working conditions).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research educational programs that formally educate supportive care providers in Saskatchewan (e.g., Sask Polytech, Saskatoon Business College, Saskatchewan Indian Institute of Technologies).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the potential earnings of supportive care provider (e.g., private versus public health care facilities, training requirements).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare direct care (e.g., provide bathing and grooming services) and indirect care (e.g., order and maintain inventory) tasks required in supportive care provider positions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze daily schedules of supportive care providers.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize the supportive care provider’s role in providing home care services.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine opportunities for volunteering in the health care in the local community.

outcomes.statement: Compare different types of health care environments staffed by supportive care providers.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 40: Types of Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 39

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Distinguish between regulated and supportive care providers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the benefits and challenges encountered by supportive care provider in different types of settings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the advantages and disadvantages of each workplace (e.g., special care homes, hospitals, respite care settings).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the process to apply for a licence to operate a private personal care home.

outcomes.statement: Examine the structure of the Canadian health care system.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 41: Canadian Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research historical aspects of Medicare in Canada and how it has evolved.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Interpret the five principles of Medicare as listed in the Canada Health Act.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify federal, provincial and territorial roles in the Canadian health care system.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate among primary, secondary and tertiary health care deliveries.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the advantages and disadvantages of private and publicly funded health care services.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare the Canadian determinants of health with the World Health Organization determinants of health.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the structure of the provincial health care system.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 42: Provincial Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the provincial government responsibilities to Canada’s health care system.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the structure of the Saskatchewan Health Authority.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify principles of patient-centered care (e.g., dignity, independence, individualized care, preferences, privacy, safety) in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the influence of Tommy Douglas and his Medicare model for health care in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research challenges with Saskatchewan’s present provincial health care model (e.g., alternative care, home care, rural and remote communities, aging population).

outcomes.statement: Investigate health care services for First Nations, Métis and Inuit people in Canada.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 43: Indigenous Health Care (Core For Supportive Care Focus) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 41

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s Calls to Action related to health (e.g., numbers 18-24).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the origins of the relationship between federal health services and First Nations and Métis people (e.g., Treaty negotiations, Northern Intertribal Health Authority).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the Non-insured Health Benefits Program for First Nations peoples registered under the Indian Act.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore Métis, Non-Status and Inuit health coverage in Canada.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the historical significance of Jordan’s Principle and the impact on health services.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate how the federal and provincial governments collaborate to provide funding for First Nations to access health care.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore access to health care in remote areas.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate issues related to diabetes in Indigenous communities.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore health care clauses in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP) Act related to Bill C-15.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research options for First Nations to choose health self-governance in Canada.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Investigate ways of actualizing the roles of Indigenous Elders and Knowledge Keepers in the health care system.

outcomes.statement: Recognize patients’ rights in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 44: Patients’ Rights (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the basic human rights protected by the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms (e.g., the right to vote, the right to life, liberty and security, the right to equality before and under the law).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe patient rights in Saskatchewan health care environments (e.g., the right to privacy and confidentially, the right to give or withhold consent, the right to autonomy).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate patient family centered care and person-centered care principles in Saskatchewan (e.g., dignity and respect, information sharing, participation, collaboration).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify ways supportive care providers demonstrate respect for their patients’ rights.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research laws and regulations that impact patient’s rights in health care environments.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore ways for patients to receive health care services in their primary language to remove language barriers.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the work environment of acute care settings.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 45: Acute Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 40

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate acute care.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the challenges of working in acute care as a supportive care provider.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the supportive care provider’s responsibilities for physical examinations (e.g., collect linens, collect examination equipment, measure vital signs).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the different types of surgeries (i.e., elective, urgent, emergency) and their purposes (i.e., diagnostic, reconstructive, curative).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the supportive care provider’s role in supporting psychological care in acute care settings (e.g., listen to the patient about their fears, refer questions about the surgery to the nurse).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the steps and procedures involved in the pre-operative and postoperative periods.

outcomes.statement: Explore effective communication skills in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 46: Communication in Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the importance of compassion when providing care to patients with communication impairments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to communicate with a patient who is dissatisfied with their care (e.g., recognize the source of frustration, treat the patient with respect and dignity, stay calm and professional, listen and use silence, leave for personal safety).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Model how to explain procedures and tasks to patients (e.g., put the patient at ease, start with easy steps, give time for practice).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain ways to effectively communicate with patients living with dementia (e.g., minimize competing noises, speak clearly and calmly, use short sentences, use humor, have one caregiver speaking at a time).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate conflict resolution strategies for conflicts with co-workers, patients and families (e.g., arrange to speak in a neutral area, identify concerning behaviours, refrain from discussing details of discussion with other co-workers).

outcomes.statement: Explore the roles and responsibilities of health care teams.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 47: Teamwork in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research how a health care team is created.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits and challenges of interprofessional health care teams.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the roles of various health care team members (e.g., registered nurse, physiotherapist, social worker, doctor, family member).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the supportive care provider’s role on the health care team.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare how teams function in different public and private health care environments (e.g., private personal care homes, long term care, hospital care).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine how the health care team can provide person-centered care (e.g. honouring patient perspectives, sharing information with patients and families, encouraging families in the decision making process).

outcomes.statement: Examine how to plan, report and record patient care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 48: Care Planning and Reporting (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 47

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the function of the care plan.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine the steps in the care planning process in health care environments and in the community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the supportive care provider’s role in the care planning process.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between objective data (i.e., information gathered based on sight, sound, smell) and subjective data (i.e., information based on patient’s report but not directly observed by others).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the criteria of an effective observation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the functions of a patient’s chart (e.g., communication, planning patient care, accountability).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the types of documents found in a patient’s chart (e.g., data forms, assessment forms, care plans, progress notes).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the types of information supportive care providers are expected to report (e.g., physical and psychological changes, nutrition, mobility, glucose-levels, report facts and not feelings).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of the 24-hour clock.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain how to respect confidentiality in all aspects of a patient’s care.

outcomes.statement: Explore stress and fatigue management strategies for workers in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 49: Employee Stress and Fatigue in Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between eustress (i.e., healthy stress that gives a sense of fulfillment), acute stress (short in duration) and chronic stress (ongoing).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how stress can affect all dimensions of health.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the physical and emotional-behavioural signs of stress (e.g., rapid pulse, increased blood pressure, nausea, irritability, burnout, anxiety).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of burnout.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore strategies to manage stress in the workplace (e.g., develop selfawareness, take care of personal needs, think positively, ask for help, practise calming exercises).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify factors that contribute to fatigue in the work environment (e.g., personal stress, work overload, scheduling, shift work).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the effects of fatigue on role performance and injury prevention for self and patients.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe strategies for preventing fatigue.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate strategies to achieve work-life balance as a supportive care provider.

outcomes.statement: Explore the contemporary meaning and historical origins of medical terminology.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 50: Medical Terminology (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify word parts such as prefixes, roots, suffixes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize the meanings of common Greek and Latin prefixes, roots and suffixes on which many medical terms are based.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Combine word elements to form medical terms (e.g., dys-difficult and pneabreathing become dyspnea, meaning difficulty in breathing)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate programs or courses that offer instruction on medical terminology in the local community.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Interpret medical reference points including anatomical body planes, anatomical directional terms, body cavities and abdominal regions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify and define some common abbreviation used in health care (e.g., BM – bowel movement, Dx – diagnosis, FBS - fasting blood sugar).

outcomes.statement: Explore home management tasks.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 51: Home Management (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List the possible duties of a supportive care providers in helping with home management (e.g., cleaning, doing laundry, taking care of pets, watering plants).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify payment options for home management services (e.g., private or provincial or territorial funding).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Review time management skills for accomplishing tasks (e.g., establish priorities, put patient needs first, develop routines, prepare all necessary equipment).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate adherence to cleaning guidelines (e.g., clear away clutter, work from higher to lower, work from far to near, work from cleanest to dirtiest).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) procedures.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate the quality of cleaning equipment such as rags, mops, vacuums and detergents.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate how to use cleaning supplies safely (e.g., wear appropriate personal protective equipment, store products in original containers, do not mix products).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the steps for cleaning bedrooms, living rooms, kitchens and bathrooms.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper use of a laundry machine.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate ways to care for garments and linens (e.g., removing stains, folding, ironing).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss how to respond to a patient who requests tasks that are not on the care plan.

outcomes.statement: Examine ways to care for older persons.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 52: Caring for Older Persons (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the emotional (e.g., loneliness, depression, joy) and social changes (e.g., retirement, reduced income, social relationships, death of a significant other, children as caregivers) that occur with aging.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the concept of aging in place.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize the signs of depression in older persons.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the physical changes that occur with aging in various body systems (e.g., musculoskeletal system, nervous system, circulatory systems).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain how to be sensitive to older persons from various cultures in a health care facility or in the home.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate ways to acknowledge life experiences of patients (e.g., identifying previous occupation, constructing memory boxes).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate ways to respect possibly traumatic lived experiences of older persons (e.g., veterans, survivors of residential schools, the Holocaust or the Great Depression).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the possible linguistic needs of older persons in health care facilities.

outcomes.statement: Examine factors related to dementia in adult patients.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 53: Dementia (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 52

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between forgetfulness and dementia.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Distinguish between disorientation, delirium and dementia.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify symptoms that could mimic those of dementia (e.g., dehydration, urinary tract infection, mood changes).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare normal and abnormal mental changes related to aging.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the signs and symptoms of dementia (e.g., forgetting names, misplacing items, becoming lost in familiar settings).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the different forms, causes and stages of dementia.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe how to support a patient living with dementia (e.g., participate in introductions at every visit, talk about plans for the day, frequently remind the patient of their location).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine why depression is often associated with dementia.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the emotional requirements of the patient diagnosed with dementia.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the role of the family in the care of the patient diagnosed with dementia.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research the impact of caring for family members with dementia on primary caregivers.

outcomes.statement: Investigate ways to support mental health of adults in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 54: Mental Health in Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research one or more mental health disorders such as acquired brain injuries, anxiety, depressive disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorders, schizophrenia spectrum disorders and trauma and stressor-related disorders.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine causes, signs and symptoms of depression.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss care strategies to support patients with depression.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how to support patients with mental health disorders.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that may contribute to mental health disorders (e.g., biological factors, childhood experiences, stressful life events, diet).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the effects of mental health disorders on families (e.g., guilt, blame, finances).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate local adult community mental health services.

outcomes.statement: Recognize the importance of exercise and activity for patients on bed rest.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 55: Exercise and Activity for Patients on Bed Rest (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe reasons why patients may require bed rest.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate among different types of bed rest (e.g., strict bed rest, bed rest with commode privileges, bed rest with bathroom privileges).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the complications of bed rest (e.g., contracture, muscle atrophy, hypotension) and how to prevent them (e.g., moving the patient every two hours).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize the devices (e.g., bed boards, foot boards, trochanter rolls, splints, trapeze) used to support and maintain body alignment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate a personal range of motion exercises (e.g., abduction, adduction, extension, flexion, hyperextension, rotation).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore range of motion activities that could be offered in long-term care facilities for full-time wheelchair users.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the social and emotional benefits of exercise and activity for patients on bed rest.

outcomes.statement: Observe how to position, transfer and lift a patient.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 56: Transfers and Lifts (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate different types of bed positions (e.g., Fowler’s position, supine position, lateral position, Sim’s position, prone position, sitting position).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify positioning requirements in a care plan directive.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize tools (e.g., fan-folded turning pad, slider sheet, transfer belt, transfer board) used to move a patient safely.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate programs and services that provide training for transfers, lifts, and repositioning (e.g., Transferring, Lifting and Repositioning training).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research frequent injuries (e.g., back, shoulder and psychological injuries) for health care providers related to lifts and transfers.

outcomes.statement: Recognize the importance of personal hygiene in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 57: Personal Hygiene (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of personal hygiene for patients and care providers in health care environments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine daily care routines including morning care, afternoon care and evening care.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how to assist with personal hygiene while considering the patient’s dignity, independence, individualized care, preferences, privacy and safety.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe oral hygiene and the observations to report to the care team.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine ways to support good oral health.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the labelling process for personal items (e.g., clothing, glasses, blankets, dentures) in health care environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the guidelines for bathing (e.g., collect all needed items before the bath, provide for privacy, protect from burns and scalds).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe compassionate caring for the patient receiving assistance with bathing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify the safety precautions for patients taking tub baths or showers.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine safe practices for caregivers providing personal hygiene services.

outcomes.statement: Investigate infection prevention strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 58: Infection Prevention (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of infection (e.g., fever and chills, nausea, rash).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine ways in which microbes are transmitted (e.g., the chain of infection) and steps to limit transmission.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss risk factors for infection (e.g., stress, poor nutrition, lack of sleep).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify routine immunizations for infection prevention.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper handwashing, cleaning and disinfection techniques.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate donning and doffing of personal protective equipment (e.g., masks, gloves, gowns).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the risks to supportive care providers and patients when infection control is not adhered to (e.g., spread of disease to a more compromised population).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research disease outbreaks including pandemic and epidemic diseases that have had significant effects on the general population past and present.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the role and responsibilities supportive care providers in preventing the spread of infection.

outcomes.statement: Examine safety measures and procedures in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 59: Safety Measures and Procedures in Health Care (Core for Supportive Care Focus) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List the risk factors for incidents (e.g., distracted or fatigued caregivers, medication, age, patients with vision, hearing or mobility challenges).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how the proper use of specialized equipment (e.g., call bells, bed rails, hand rails) can promote patient safety.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the safety measures to prevent falls, poisoning, suffocation and burns in older adults.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate health care codes that support safety (e.g., code red, blue, burgundy, white).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe guidelines to follow for emergency preparedness (e.g., in case of fire, weather event, lock down) in a health care environment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe safety guidelines to follow when using electrical equipment such as hair dryers, curling irons and electric razors with patients in health care environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain household management safety, including guidelines for dealing with pest infestations, linen and light housekeeping.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the protocol to dispose of contaminated items or waste, including sharp objects.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe measures to ensure personal safety when at work in a health care environment (e.g., when entering a patient’s home, choice of clothing and jewelry).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the risks associated with working alone with a patient and how they can be mitigated.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the steps to reporting a workplace injury.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Explain how various emotions and reactions may block effective responses.

outcomes.statement: Apply bed making techniques.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 60: Bed Making (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain how to handle linen according to the rules of standard practice (e.g., frequency of changes, order of application to bed, manipulation of the linen).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the types of bed linens used when making a patient’s bed.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize the different types of incontinence pads (e.g., reusable, disposable).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe safety measures for bed making.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the differences between open beds (i.e., shortly before the bed is to be occupied), closed beds (i.e., expected to be unoccupied for several hours or days) and occupied beds (i.e., a bed being made while the patient is in the bed).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate the making of an open and a closed bed.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate grooming and dressing strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 61: Grooming and Dressing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of hair care and shaving.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the factors that affect hair care.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize conditions that may be related to a patient’s hair care plan such as alopecia, dandruff and pediculosis.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how to care for matted and tangled hair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how to provide culturally sensitive grooming.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe how to shampoo hair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: List the steps to shave a patient.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify safety considerations related to basic nail care.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research training opportunities to learn about appropriate nail and foot care procedures.
