evidence.observation: The outcomes page groups the outcomes under 3 unit headings.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze how authors/creators develop character, conflict (e.g., character vs. self, character vs. character, character vs. society, character vs. nature), setting and point of view in fiction and non-fiction texts to express worldviews, values, or social tensions across cultural, historical or geographical contexts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Interpret fiction and non-fiction texts by inferring multiple plausible meanings or perspectives, explaining how context and textual evidence shape interpretation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze how fiction and non-fiction texts use structure, evidence, tone and rhetorical devices (e.g., appeals, repetition, direct address) to inform, provoke thought or persuade.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze how an author’s/creator’s stance, bias or context influence interpretation of fiction and non-fiction texts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine connections among ideas, observations, opinions, themes and emotions across a variety of texts from diverse voices.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare how different text forms (e.g., poem, essay, oral teaching) explore similar social issues or themes and assess how the form impacts interpretation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze how the mode of communication influences the message and impacts the audience’s understanding, perception, emotional response and engagement (see Appendix A).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply comprehension and metacognitive strategies (e.g., previewing, questioning, visualizing) to support the construction of meaning across modalities and text types (see Appendix B and Appendix C).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect on how texts raise questions or offer insights about identity, social responsibility or social agency (action).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Develop original descriptive, narrative, poetic, expository and persuasive compositions that demonstrate understanding of genre-specific purposes, structures and language features (see Appendices D-H).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Experiment with various modalities (e.g., written, oral, visual, multimodal) to determine which one(s) best supports the purpose, audience and message of the composition.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compose both fiction and non-fiction texts, thoughtfully considering the elements of each form, such as fact-based development in non-fiction and imaginative techniques in fiction.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Integrate multimodal elements (e.g., sound, image, movement, visual design) thoughtfully when composing in hybrid formats to enhance the delivery of the intended message.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop compositions that explore personal and collective identities, promote social responsibility and inspire social agency (action).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Revise compositions for clarity, coherence and impact, considering how effectively genre and form are aligned to audience and purpose.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop composition stamina by creating a longer-form text that sustains ideas, organization, purpose and audience engagement across the whole composition.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Combine genre-specific features (e.g., character development in narrative, rhetorical appeals in persuasion, vivid imagery in description) to shape the composition’s tone, structure and impact (see Appendices D-H).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Analyze how form, genre, audience and purpose shape the creative choices made throughout the composition process.

outcomes.statement: Reflect on the role of stories, narratives and oral traditions in expressing diverse values and worldviews from across the globe, including Indigenous perspectives.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine how stories, narratives and oral traditions convey knowledge, values and teachings within specific cultures or communities.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine how the structure (e.g., cyclical, linear) and delivery (e.g., relational/ community/ cultural context) of stories, narratives and oral traditions are connected to the worldview they express.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore how stories, narratives and oral traditions from across the globe convey ecological, spiritual or social teachings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how personal understanding of a story, narrative or oral tradition shifts when considering the cultural, historical or geographical context in which it was created or shared.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate how stories, narratives and oral traditions reflect cultural identity, community values and ways of knowing across global Indigenous and non-Indigenous contexts.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on the ethical responsibilities of engaging with global stories, narratives and oral traditions, especially when learners are outside the culture of origin.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how stories, narratives and oral traditions from across the globe can broaden understanding of diverse perspectives, experiences and ways of knowing.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on how exploring global stories, narratives and oral traditions can expand one’s worldview (e.g., recognizing multiple ways of understanding, questioning previously held assumptions, deepening understanding of different lived experiences).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain how stories, narratives and oral traditions from diverse cultures can reveal both shared human experiences and distinct cultural perspectives.

outcomes.statement: Reflect on how personal experiences, social contexts and cultural backgrounds influence both the interpretation of texts and creation of compositions.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on how one’s lived experiences, values or worldview influence decisions about form, tone, genre and audience in original compositions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore how cultural background or social context can influence an author’s/creator’s choices in themes, perspectives or representations within texts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine how texts by authors/creators with diverse backgrounds or lived experiences can expand or shift personal or collective viewpoints on social issues, cultural practices or historical events.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Reflect on the responsibility authors/creators hold when representing identities, cultures and experiences that differ from their own.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain how interpretations of a text may differ across individuals, communities or time periods due to personal, cultural, social or historical contexts.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine how understanding an author’s/creator’s personal, social or cultural context can shape interpretation across different texts, audiences or time periods.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Incorporate personal, cultural or social context as a source of insight, voice or meaningful engagement with the audience when developing original compositions.

outcomes.statement: Analyze how authors/creators strategically integrate elements in multimodal texts to communicate ideas and engage the audience.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine how audience interpretation of multimodal texts may shift based on individual experiences, context (e.g., platform, cultural moment, target audience) or familiarity with various modes.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine how multimodal elements influence audience engagement, emotional response or interpretation of perspectives, biases or calls to action (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze how specific design principles (e.g., colour, texture, size, proximity, repetition) guide viewer’s attention and emphasize key ideas (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the ethical responsibility of creators (e.g., crediting authors/creators, respectful representations, considering privacy and consent) when selecting, editing or combining multimodal elements (e.g., images, sound, captions, pacing, layout, AI-generated elements), considering how these choices may shape audience interpretation, emotion or trust.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Evaluate how the interaction between elements (e.g., how audio complements visuals, how text layout affects pacing) either strengthens or detracts from the overall message (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate how creators layer modes (e.g., narration with archival footage, animation with text overlays) to enhance accessibility, emotional resonance, or complexity of message.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze how mentor multimodal compositions position the audience (e.g., active participants, witnesses, learners, critics) through intentional design choices, such as framing, voiceover, interactive features or sequencing of elements.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Compare multimodal texts that address a similar topic to analyze how their composition choices affect meaning and engagement.

outcomes.statement: Combine multimodal elements strategically to convey messages with clarity, emotion and intention.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Plan multimodal compositions by selecting and intentionally combining elements (e.g., text, visuals, sound, movement) in ways that support purpose, audience, message and tone across modes (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Combine modes thoughtfully (e.g., visual imagery, sound effects, text, movement, narration) to guide the audience’s attention, deepen understanding and strengthen accessibility or emotional effect (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Combine design features (e.g., colour palettes, font size and style, white space, transitions, image placement) to create emphasis, rhythm or emotion (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Reflect on how changes in one element (e.g., altering tone of voice, background visuals) influence the interpretation of other elements and the overall cohesion of the composition.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Revise compositions to improve the relationship between elements, ensuring that each serves a clear purpose within the whole.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply accessibility strategies when combining modes (e.g., using captions with video, high contrast visuals with clear text, alt-text for images) to ensure clarity, usability and inclusion for all audiences (see Appendix K).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Consider cultural diversity, emotional safety and audience perspectives when making design choices, reflecting on how language, imagery and form may include, exclude or impact audiences.

outcomes.statement: Analyze how form, style, tone, structure, purpose and language features of different genres can shape meaning and enhance audience impact.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze the purpose and functions of descriptive, narrative, poetic, expository and persuasive genres (see Appendices D-H).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze how structural choices (e.g., spatial order in descriptive, cause-effect in expository) shape the clarity and emotional impact of each genre (see Appendices D-H).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine how language features such as imagery, rhetorical appeals, figurative language, sentence variety and diction serve different purposes within and across genres.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how perceived neutrality in genres, such as expository or informational writing, may still reflect an author’s/creator’s bias, framing choices or selective evidence that influence audience interpretation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain genre-specific strategies in mentor texts and how they connect to the message, theme or argument.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze how genre language features engage audiences differently through mood, tone, voice and stylistic conventions (see Appendices D-H).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how genre language features adapt to different formats (e.g., oral retellings, multimodal representations, digital compositions) while maintaining core genre characteristics.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Compare how similar thematic topics (e.g., injustice, joy, doubts) are explored through different genres and how genre-specific choices affect audience interpretation and impact.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain how genre expectations can be deliberately followed, blended or subverted to enhance impact or convey complex meaning.

outcomes.statement: Experiment with form, style, tone, structure and language features in original descriptive, narrative, poetic, expository and persuasive compositions to suit different purposes and audiences.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Experiment with different perspectives (e.g., shifting between first-person, second-person, or third-person point of view; retelling an event from another character’s perspective; using limited, omniscient or unreliable narration) to explore how voice shapes audience engagement and interpretation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Disrupt conventional structures (e.g., using nonlinear timelines, in medias res openings, cliffhangers, fragmented or reverse order) to test how sequencing affects tension, pacing and clarity.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Transform an existing text or idea into a new form (e.g., found poem from a news article; personal story retold in dramatic monologue; visual collage from an essay) to explore meaning-making across genre and modes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Experiment with multimodal or non-verbal storytelling techniques to express ideas when language is limited, absent or intentionally minimized.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Transform language creatively (e.g., vernacular, repetition, dialect, sensory imagery, unexpected word pairings) to evoke tone, mood, or emotion appropriate to genre and audience.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Incorporate elements like dialogue, inner monologue, or contrasting character voices to build tension, reveal motivation or develop complex conflict.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore form and style with low-stakes composition tasks (e.g., timed creative writes, collaborative genre mashups, character improvisations) without the pressure of perfection.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on how experimentation helped clarify intention, shift audience impact or open new possibilities for voice and genre.

outcomes.statement: Analyze how craft techniques enhance the meaning and impact of texts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine specific author/creator moves (e.g., diction, metaphor, repetition, imagery, fragmented sentences, shifts in tone, strategic dialogue) that shape tone and mood.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze how craft techniques in descriptive texts (e.g., sensory detail, figurative language, spatial or chronological structure, selective focus) evoke emotion, create atmosphere or highlight significance (see Appendix D).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze how craft techniques in narrative texts (e.g., character and plot development, point of view, dialogue, flashbacks, setting, pacing, text features, anecdote, organizational structure, evidence selection) immerse the reader and build engagement (see Appendix E).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze how craft techniques in poetic texts (e.g., line breaks, stanza structure, repetition, rhythm, figurative language, imagery, sound devices) create emotion and emphasis (see Appendix F).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze how craft techniques in expository texts (e.g., organizational structure, text features, rhetorical questions, anecdotal examples, tone) clarify ideas and guide understanding (see Appendix G).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze how craft techniques in persuasive texts (e.g., counterarguments, rhetorical devices), including rhetorical appeals (i.e., ethos, pathos, logos, kairos, telos) influence beliefs, emotions or actions (see Appendix H).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Evaluate how strategies in oral texts (e.g., inflection, pacing, volume, pausing, emphasis) affect audience engagement and interpretation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze how non-verbal craft techniques (e.g., facial expressions, gestures, posture, eye contact) contribute to meaning, tone, and audience impact in live or recorded performances, speeches and oral storytelling.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Evaluate how creators use intentional design choices (e.g., sequencing, layout, white space, sound, visual composition) to enhance clarity, atmosphere or argument strength.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze how sentence- and word-level craft techniques (e.g., parallelism, rule of three, syntactic variation, repetition of key terms or structures, parts of speech) influence emphasis, rhythm, clarity, tone, and persuasive or expressive impact across texts.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Analyze how different authors/creators approach similar themes, issues or ideas through distinct stylistic and structural decisions (e.g., extended metaphors, different points of view).

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Explain how diverse languages (e.g., signed, spoken, and multilingual language use) and modes of communication (e.g., captions, visual supports) convey meaning and emotion in compositions.

outcomes.statement: Use craft techniques to enhance the quality, style and impact of original compositions.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply a variety of craft techniques from mentor texts to suit audience, genre and purpose (see Appendices D-H).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Apply descriptive techniques (e.g., sensory detail, figurative language, spatial or chronological structure, selective focus) to evoke emotion, create atmosphere or highlight significance (see Appendix D).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Apply narrative techniques (e.g., character and plot development, point of view, dialogue, flashbacks, setting, pacing) to immerse the audience and build narrative tension (see Appendix E).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply poetic techniques (e.g., line breaks, stanza structure, repetition, rhythm, figurative language, imagery, sound devices) to create tone, emotion and emphasis (see Appendix F).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply expository techniques (e.g., organizational structure, text features, rhetorical questions, anecdotal examples, tone) to clarify complex ideas and guide reader understanding (see Appendix G).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply persuasive techniques (e.g., rhetorical appeals, direct address, repetition, tone, purposeful sentence structure) to influence thinking and action (see Appendix H).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Apply oral delivery strategies (e.g., inflection, pacing, volume, pausing, emphasis) to enhance clarity, rhythm and emotional impact in original compositions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply non-verbal strategies (e.g., facial expressions, gestures, posture, eye contact) to reinforce tone, clarify meaning and strengthen audience engagement in original compositions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Justify which craft techniques were most effective in achieving the intended impact of original compositions.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Apply sentence- and word-level craft techniques (e.g., parallelism, rule of three, sentence length and variety, repetition, strategic word choice, syntactic variation) to strengthen emphasis, rhythm, clarity, tone and meaning in original compositions.

outcomes.statement: Apply comprehension and metacognitive strategies that deepen understanding and analysis when reading, listening and viewing.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply global, problem-solving and support strategies to monitor learning and deepen comprehension when reading, listening and viewing (see Appendix B and Appendix C).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Make and refine predictions before and during reading, listening, or viewing by drawing on titles, genre features, prior knowledge and contextual clues.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Establish a specific purpose before reading, listening, and viewing (e.g., understanding argument, identifying genre features, evaluating author's stance) and adjust strategies (e.g., shifting from skimming to close reading when a key argument or tone shift appears) as new information is encountered.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify when understanding breaks down and use strategies (e.g., re-reading, summarizing, slowing down pace, asking questions for clarification) to improve comprehension.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply morphology strategies by analyzing word parts (i.e., roots, prefixes, suffixes) to decode unfamiliar vocabulary and enhance comprehension.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Engage with texts multiple times for distinct purposes (e.g., first encounter for basic comprehension, second for analyzing structure or language features, third for interpreting author’s/creator’s craft, tone or deeper meanings).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze how recognizing genre-specific craft techniques during reading, listening or viewing (e.g., narrative suspense, persuasive appeals, poetic repetition) enhances comprehension, supports interpretation and deepens awareness of purpose and audience impact.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Use support strategies during and after reading, listening or viewing (e.g., annotating texts, posing questions, taking structured notes, using graphic organizers) to map key ideas and analyze texts.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Visualize complex descriptions or abstract ideas that enhance understanding of challenging sections.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect on the effectiveness of personal comprehension strategies post-task by identifying what worked, what was challenging and setting specific future goals.

outcomes.statement: Use a variety of writing and design processes to thoughtfully plan, develop, revise and refine original compositions.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore multiple ideas, forms and craft techniques through a variety of low-stakes composition processes (e.g., quick writes, spoken brainstorms, imitation writing).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Plan original written, oral, visual and multimodal compositions using strategies (e.g., brainstorming, mind-mapping, sketching, discussion or inquiry questions) to generate ideas, clarify purpose and consider audience.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Organize ideas intentionally during planning by selecting appropriate structures, modalities, and design elements suited to the intended genre (e.g., sensory details, narrative pacing, logical organization, figurative language), purpose (e.g., to entertain, to persuade) and audience.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Experiment with early drafts by using a variety of design processes (e.g., storyboard, speech annotations, Venn diagram) to test ideas, structures and genre techniques.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Revise original compositions meaningfully by reworking content, structure, form, style or mode based on self-assessment, peer feedback and evolving clarity of purpose.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Refine original compositions by polishing language, improving coherence, fine-tuning transitions, clarifying key ideas, and aligning form and tone precisely to purpose and audience.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Revise titles in original compositions to align with purpose and genre and enhance the audience's engagement or interpretation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Finalize original compositions for the intended audience, considering how final design, medium, and presentation choices impact meaning, accessibility and emotional resonance.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect on feedback and creative intentions to determine which suggestions enhance clarity, strengthen purpose, or improve audience impact, and make intentional decisions about what to revise, retain, or reject based on creative vision.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Revise recursively by revisiting ideas, structure and techniques at multiple stages to refine meaning and expression over time.

outcomes.statement: Apply appropriate spelling, grammar, punctuation and language conventions according to genre, purpose and audience.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply grammar, syntax, punctuation and spelling conventions to enhance clarity and coherence in original compositions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Adjust use of language conventions based on purpose, audience and genre (e.g., formal conventions for academic essays; strategic flexibility for creative, spoken word, or informal compositions).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use morphological strategies (i.e., analyzing roots, prefixes and suffixes) to spell complex words accurately and to expand academic vocabulary.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Edit drafts purposefully to correct errors in spelling, punctuation and grammar, focusing on patterns of strength and recurring areas for improvement.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Utilize punctuation and syntax intentionally to control pacing, emphasis and tone in compositions (e.g., varied sentence lengths, line breaks, strategic use of commas, dashes, pauses).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Organize ideas into cohesive sections (e.g., paragraphs, scenes, stanzas, frames, slides) that reflect purposeful shifts in focus, topic, speaker, time, or tone to support clarity, coherence and audience understanding in original compositions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Reflect on how choices in tone, formality and language precision affect audience perception and comprehension.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recognize and discuss the evolving nature of language conventions across different cultural, social and digital contexts (e.g., how African American Vernacular English has grammatical rules distinct from Standard American English; how professional vs. peer dialogue changes in tone, formality and structure; how emojis, hashtags, or acronyms can shift meaning and tone).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Use appropriate citation styles in formal writing (e.g., MLA for literary and artistic analysis; APA for research, informational, or social science-related texts), selecting format based on context, discipline and audience.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the credibility and effectiveness of information presented in a range of texts, including media and digital texts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze factors that contribute to credibility (e.g., author expertise, institutional affiliation, purpose, transparency of sourcing) and reliability (e.g., accuracy of information, use of evidence, consistency across sources).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze factors that contribute to a lack of credibility (e.g., unclear authorship, lack of expertise, missing source information, obvious bias, lack of transparency, misleading intent) and reliability (e.g., inaccurate information, unsupported claims, limited evidence, outdated information, inconsistency across sources).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze how medium, modality, platform and publication context (e.g., independent journalism vs. sponsored content, news article vs. influencer post, date of publication) influence the credibility, reliability and perceived objectivity of a text.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how persuasive techniques (e.g., loaded or emotional language, selective use of statistics, repetition, jargon, propaganda, oversimplification) can distort facts, influence perception or compromise the objectivity of information.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze how visual or multimodal elements (e.g., image selection, layout, sound design, captioning) shape the perceived trustworthiness and tone of a source.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare sources on the same topic to identify conflicting information, omissions or alignment of facts, and evaluate how these influence understanding and interpretation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how personal interest, prior knowledge, bias or media habits may influence one’s evaluation of a source and identify ways to approach information more critically.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on which additional sources or perspectives are needed to deepen understanding.

outcomes.statement: Integrate reliable and credible evidence from multiple sources to support claims.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Integrate evidence from a range of credible and reliable sources (e.g., peer-reviewed research, teachings from Elders or Knowledge Keepers shared with permission and appropriate protocol*, verified statistics) that align with the purpose, genre and audience of the composition.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Introduce evidence with framing language that clarifies its relevance:
- “According to…”
- “As shared in the interview with…”
- “This demonstrates that…”
- “The author suggests...”
- “The situation shows...”
- “The actions of the character demonstrate...”.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the function of each piece of evidence by explaining how it strengthens reasoning, anticipates counterarguments, deepens the central message, theme or argument, or influences audience interpretation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply a range of evidence integration strategies (e.g., embedding, summarizing, paraphrasing, quoting with a colon or signal phrase) to preserve originality and avoid over-reliance on source material.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text:
Apply different strategies for tracking and attributing sources (e.g., primary, secondary, print, scholarly, AI) depending on context:
- In academic or research-based compositions, use appropriate citation styles (e.g., MLA for literary analysis, APA for informational texts).
- In informal, creative or oral compositions, attribute ideas through oral acknowledgments, captions, credits or notes in accompanying materials.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Revise compositions to maintain clarity and accuracy when integrating evidence, ensuring evidence is connected to claims and explained in relation to purpose.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Distinguish between types of evidence (e.g., anecdotal, literary, empirical, statistical, testimonial) and apply each intentionally to strengthen reasoning and influence audience interpretation.

outcomes.statement: Develop a central message, theme or argument by exploring a topic and narrowing its scope.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a fully developed theme (e.g., love becomes destructive when rooted in fear) beyond a thematic topic (e.g., love).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Generate open-ended questions that reflect personal, societal or literary concerns (e.g., Who am I becoming? What shapes my values? How do we respond to fear or hope?).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Narrow a topic by exploring patterns, tensions or perspectives that emerge across texts or experiences, using these insights to shape a precise central message, theme or argument.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Select a genre and form that best aligns with a narrowed focus, considering how structure, modality and voice can amplify the intended impact (e.g., argument in editorial form, theme in short story, message in visual collage).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Refine the central message, theme or argument by ensuring it is reflected not only in content, but in aesthetic or craft techniques (e.g., repetition in spoken word poetry; visual symbolism in film; motif in prose).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Ensure each section, paragraph or design element contributes meaningfully to the overall message, avoiding content that distracts or contradicts the intended purpose.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Revise to improve clarity, emotional resonance and coherence, assessing whether the narrowed focus remains visible and sustained throughout the piece.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Consider how cultural, social, historical and personal lenses can shape how audiences interpret the central message, theme or argument and revise to strengthen clarity, relevance, or resonance across diverse contexts.

outcomes.statement: Engage with others in respectful, focused dialogue to foster critical thinking, negotiate interpretations and deepen comprehension.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Pose purposeful, open-ended questions that challenge assumptions, uncover ambiguities or invite multiple interpretations of a composition, idea or theme (see Appendix I).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Justify interpretations or creative decisions with evidence from multiple sources (e.g., texts, prior discussions, personal experience) while engaging in thoughtful exchanges that test the strength and limitations of those interpretations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Engage in a variety of collaborative discussion formats (e.g., small group jigsaw, role-based seminars, collaborative inquiry) to engage in focused dialogue and deepen understanding.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Co-construct meaning of complex texts by collaboratively exploring how different interpretations arise from varied lenses, contexts or textual elements and by negotiating shared or divergent understandings of complex texts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Contribute to collaborative discussions by acknowledging others’ contributions, asking clarifying questions and connecting multiple perspectives.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate respect for diverse perspectives by acknowledging differing opinions and lived experiences, using inclusive language and maintaining a constructive tone during disagreement.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate awareness of group dynamics by encouraging contributions, mediating tensions and adapting communication to support productive, inclusive and critical dialogue.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Refine personal and group ideas by analyzing how feedback, disagreement or new insights reveal gaps, tensions or deeper meanings within a text, topic or discussion.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect on how collaborative dialogue shapes, expands or challenges personal thinking or comprehension.

outcomes.statement: Collaborate with others to generate ideas, organize and revise original compositions, contributing ideas and feedback to improve clarity, effectiveness and impact.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate and build ideas with various brainstorming strategies (e.g., mentor-text inspired exercises, low-stakes compositions tasks, sketching) identifying possibilities for genre, voice, or structure.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Provide thoughtful, question-driven feedback that highlights strengths, identifies gaps and invites deeper thinking about clarity, nuance or artistic intention.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Engage in conferences to discuss creative choices, offering specific suggestions about structure, language, tone, multimodal integration or genre alignment to strengthen the logical flow and impact of original compositions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Experiment with peer-suggested feedback (e.g., altering genre, reworking perspective, shifting modality), documenting changes and analyzing how revisions improve meaning and overall effectiveness of compositions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Experiment with new techniques or structures suggested through dialogue (e.g., trying a different opening move, adjusting pacing, reordering sections) to strengthen personal compositions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on how giving and receiving feedback shapes understanding and informs decisions or goals for future compositions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Collaborate with others to generate and refine ideas for individual compositions (written, oral, visual, multimodal), expanding possibilities for audience engagement, genre exploration and clarity of purpose (See Appendix J).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Revise compositions collaboratively by incorporating techniques from mentor texts (e.g., leads, transitions, repetition), reflecting on how these choices enhance clarity or audience engagement.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Provide focused, constructive feedback (e.g., noting confusions, emotions and curiosities) to others on ways to enhance clarity, effectiveness, emotional impact or coherence in their original compositions.

outcomes.statement:
View, listen to, read, comprehend, and respond to a variety of grade-appropriate First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts that address:
- identity (e.g., Define the Individual, Negotiate the Community)
- social responsibility (e.g., Shift Centres, Blur Margins), and
- social action (agency) (e.g., Understand Beliefs, Initiate Action).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore topics and contemporary and traditional visual, oral, multimedia (including digital) and written First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts that present different viewpoints and perspectives including those that reflect the diversity of Canada and its citizens' diverse personal identities, worldviews, and backgrounds (e.g., community, culture, values, spirituality, socio-economic status, language, ability, age, gender, appearance).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze and respond to a variety of First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts representative of various time periods and of the diverse cultures and regions of Canada in order to extend understanding of the ideas, themes, and issues explored in the texts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts to identify particular perspectives presented, and the forms and stylistic means used to communicate those perspectives.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze how historical, regional, cultural, political, and social contexts and events influence the presentation and interpretation of ideas, issues, and themes in First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify connections between personal experiences and prior knowledge of language and texts to develop interpretations of a variety of First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Respond personally and critically to perspectives and styles of a variety of First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts and explain how the study of those texts enhances understanding of self, others, and Canadian identity.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze ways in which language and texts reflect and influence the values and behaviours of people and diverse communities.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify the various elements of style used in First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts, and explain how the elements help communicate meaning and enhance the effectiveness of the texts.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain how First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian texts raise awareness about a variety of regional issues, ideas, cultures, events, and people, and promote social and personal change.

outcomes.statement: View and evaluate critically information and ideas obtained from First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian visual and multimedia texts including an advertisement, news broadcast, poster, and film.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: View and respond to grade-appropriate visual and multimedia texts created by First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian artists and authors from various cultural communities.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Select deliberately and use effectively a variety of before (page 27), during (page 28), and after (page 29) strategies to construct and confirm meaning when viewing texts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use language cues and conventions (page 24) of a variety of informational and literary texts to construct and confirm meaning when viewing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Demonstrate critical viewing behaviours:
- Determine what the text is representing
- Identify and analyze how the text was constructed
- Identify the purposes, intended audiences, messages, points of view, and techniques of the text
- Infer the assumptions, interests, beliefs, and values embedded in the text, and the credibility and purpose of the author
- Identify and analyze speaker's, artist's, or author's tone, attitude, and bias
- Analyze how the text uses argument, images, placement, editing, and/or music for effect and impact
- Evaluate and critique the persuasive techniques including emotion and propaganda.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Evaluate critically information (i.e., whose voice is heard, whose is not) obtained from viewing a visual or multimedia text.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain and evaluate the effectiveness of persuasive strategies and techniques in a range of visual and multimedia texts.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Infer point of view and biases explicit in visual and multimedia texts.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze, compare, and critique different visual and multimedia presentations of the same ideas, information, or issues.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the accuracy and balance of information presented in visual and multimedia texts.

outcomes.statement: Listen to, comprehend, and develop coherent and plausible interpretations of grade-appropriate literary and informational texts created by First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian speakers and authors from various communities.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Listen to, respond to, and interpret oral texts created by First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian speakers and authors from various cultural communities.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Select deliberately and use effectively a variety of before (page 27), during (page 28), and after (page 29) strategies to construct and confirm meaning when listening to texts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use language cues and conventions (page 24) of a variety of informational and literary texts to construct and confirm meaning when listening.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Demonstrate critical listening behaviours:
- Concentrate, focus, and attend
- Filter distractions and recognize factors that interfere with effective listening, including personal biases
- Identify the thesis of a speech and determine the essential elements that develop the thesis
- Recognize speaker's values, perspective, biases, and tone
- Analyze explicit and implicit messages/concepts, viewpoints, theme, and tone
- Recognize overall plan or organization including transitional expressions
- Distinguish between emotional appeal and reasoned argument
- Evaluate and verify facts and arguments
- Identify logical fallacies in oral arguments
- Identify key allusions and symbols
- Use effective note making strategies and a variety of written or graphic forms to organize and share ideas acquired from what was listened to
- Prepare and ask relevant questions, and respond appropriately
- Analyze the overall effectiveness of the presentation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Outline and summarize an oral presentation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate proficiency in reflective, critical, empathetic, and appreciative listening.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare and contrast interpretations of oral texts with the interpretations of others and research points of contention.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Provide appropriate feedback in a variety of situations including discussions and informative, persuasive, and artistic presentations.

outcomes.statement: Read, demonstrate comprehension of, and apply knowledge from grade-appropriate informational (including editorials, reviews, and articles) and literary (including fiction, script, poetry, and non-fiction) texts from First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian authors as a basis for understanding self and the multiplicity of voices and perspectives that make up Canadian culture.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Read, comprehend, and respond to informational and literary texts by First Nations, Métis, Saskatchewan, and Canadian authors, and explain how the texts represent our Canadian literary and cultural heritage.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Select deliberately and use effectively a variety of before (page 28), during (page 29), and after (page 30) strategies to construct and confirm meaning when reading texts.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use language cues and conventions (page 24) of a variety of informational and literary texts to construct and confirm meaning when reading.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Demonstrate critical reading behaviours to analyze meanings, ideas, language, and literary quality in a range of contemporary and historical texts:
- Establish a purpose for reading such as to learn, interpret, andenjoy
- Skim, scan, and read closely
- Identify and analyze explicit and implicit messages, viewpoints, and concepts
- Analyze the ways in which a text's organizational structure and elements support or confound its purpose
- Relate understanding of a range of texts to personal experience, purposes, audience, and other texts
- Evaluate accuracy (e.g., differentiate fact from opinion), credibility, logic, and usefulness of ideas and information presented
- Differentiate between literal and figurative statements
- Recognize and comprehend symbols and allusions
- Test ideas and values presented in texts
- Use note making and outlining to enhance understanding of texts.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize and evaluate major literary forms and techniques and how the forms are shaped into an artistic unit.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the elements of the authors' styles and the methods by which they are achieved.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Paraphrase the main ideas, events, or themes in a variety of sophisticated literary and informational texts, along with supportive evidence.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop coherent and plausible interpretations of a variety of sophisticated print texts.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Support a position, interpretation, or response by citing specific details, features, and ideas from what was read.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate an appreciation of the power and beauty of language, past and present, in print texts.

outcomes.statement:
Create a range of visual, multimedia, oral, and written texts that explore:
- identity (e.g., Define the Individual, Negotiate the Community),
- social responsibility (e.g., Shift Centres, Blur Margins), and
- social action (agency) (e.g., Understand Beliefs, Initiate Action).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Create a range of visual, oral, multimedia, and written texts that include the following:
- A clear thesis or main idea
- Details that logically and effectively support the thesis or main idea
- Style, voice, format, and organizational pattern appropriate to purpose and audience
- Unity, coherence, and emphasis
- A plausible and effective conclusion.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Develop independently an inquiry project relating to a particular topic or issue with reference to purpose and audience and employing a variety of research tools and resources:
- Consider own and others' expertise to explore breadth and depth of knowledge and focus inquiry or research based on parameters of task
- Formulate inquiry or research questions, and refine them through reflection and discussion of topic, purpose, and context
- Consider whether thesis claim is personally relevant, interesting, and meaningful; relevant and meaningful to the audience; aligned with purpose and goals; logical; and can be supported
- Develop and select from a repertoire of inquiry strategies, and adjust plan according to needs (audience, purpose, context)
- Evaluate and select ideas and information from prior knowledge of inquiry or research topic appropriate for audience, purpose, and perspective or focus
- Use a variety of digital and informational resources (e.g., human, libraries, databases, networks, video) to gather, evaluate, and synthesize information and perspectives to create and communicate knowledge to achieve purpose and suit audience
- Evaluate factors that affect the credibility, authenticity, accuracy, and bias of information sources
- Evaluate information for completeness, accuracy, currency, historical context, relevance, balance of perspectives, and bias
- Organize and reorganize information and ideas to clarify thinking and to achieve desired effect
- Incorporate, strategically, source material in a variety of ways including directly quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing, and using ellipses and brackets, and document sources accurately.

outcomes.statement: Create and present visual and multimedia representations including using photographs to explain a range of contemporary course-related perspectives or landscapes.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Prepare and present visual and multimedia presentations:
- Exhibit logical structures appropriate to audience, purpose, and context
- Develop a central focus and craft strong messages
- Organize ideas in logical and appropriate sequences
- Include smooth transitions
- Use a variety of forms and technologies such as sound, photographs, and models
- Understand how ideas are communicated through elements of design such as colour, shape, line, and texture
- Provide logical and convincing conclusions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Select, use, and evaluate deliberately a wide variety of before, during, and after strategies to communicate meaning when representing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Apply accurately and effectively the language cues and conventions to construct and communicate meaning when representing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Prepare a visual or multimedia presentation on a contemporary Canadian landscape or perspective:
- Develop a presentation that is appropriate to the subject, audience, and purpose, including informing, persuading, and entertaining
- Focus on main points of presentation and include only details that strongly support main points
- Use question, fact, anecdote, or visual aids to get audience's attention
- Sequence visuals in best possible order and support them with sound, maps, charts, objects, or other visual and auditory aids
- Conclude by restating main points in a memorable way
- Use posture, gestures, and facial expressions to send the same message as visuals and words.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Communicate thoughts, ideas, and feelings using two or more media.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Present information on a topic in a planned and focused group session using a variety of audio-visual aids.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Use a variety of technologies to facilitate and enhance representation including computer software and multimedia technology.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe and evaluate alternative approaches to presentations for specific audiences and purposes.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Experiment with a variety of text forms (e.g., video documentary) and techniques (e.g., dissolve, fade).

outcomes.statement: Present and express a range of ideas and information in formal (including a panel presentation and a business or community meeting) and informal (including discussions and collaborative work) situations for differing audiences and purposes.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Function both as a group member and a group leader and demonstrate effective group interaction skills and strategies:
- Demonstrate commitment and flexibility in a group and to the team's and project's goals
- Monitor own and others' contributions
- Build on others' strengths to achieve group goals by collaborating and consulting effectively with others in completing communications tasks
- Assume responsibility for roles in teams
- Represent and promote respect for contributions of other team members
- Apply a variety of strategies including formal decision-making techniques and consensus-building skills to solve problems and achieve group goals.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Select, use, and evaluate deliberately a wide variety of before, during, and after strategies to communicate meaning when speaking.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Apply accurately and effectively the language cues and conventions to construct and communicate meaning when speaking.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Create and present oral presentations:
- Employ and exhibit a logical structure appropriate to the context, audience, and purpose
- Group related ideas and maintain a consistent focus
- Include smooth transitions
- Support judgements with sound evidence and well-chosen details
- Make skillful use of rhetorical devices
- Provide coherent conclusions
- Employ appropriate eye contact, speaking rate, volume, enunciation, inflection, and gestures to communicate ideas.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text:
Prepare and participate in a panel presentation (findings from an inquiry) (e.g., dialects in Canada):
- Determine what a knowledgeable, skilled individual or expert might know
- Organize group effectively
- Give an effective introduction (chairperson or moderator introduce the topic, the members of the panel, the aspect of the topic each panel member will address, and the overall thesis of the panel presentation)
- Present, as a panelist, own section in a clear and logical manner by defining or explaining necessary terms, presenting ideas in logical order, and using and explaining examples
- Connect different sections
- Show thorough knowledge of topic
- Present an effective conclusion.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Attend a formal meeting, note aspects of formal procedure, organize, and participate in a business or community meeting:
- Practise the rules and procedures that govern business or community meetings
- Present purpose of meeting clearly, and as an individual member present one part of the background analysis of a problem (e.g., history of problem, effects of problem, causes of problem, importance of problem, evolution of problem)
- Prepare an agenda that lists the order of business (e.g., call to order, minutes of previous meeting, discussion on unfinished business, reports, new business, adjournment)
- Present one part of the background analysis and bring ideas and voices to the discussion as well as own solution to the group problem
- Participate in bringing items forward for discussion and decision (carried, defeated, tabled)
- Follow formal procedures (e.g., Robert's Rules of Order) and acknowledge role of chairperson (leads meeting, sees that everyone has an opportunity to speak , takes the votes, and ensures that minutes are recorded).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate a willingness to explore diverse perspectives to develop and modify viewpoints.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the value, limitations, and ethical issues associated with collaborative work.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Interact purposefully, confidently, and ethically in a variety of interpersonal and electronic school and community contexts.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and adjust oral presentation elements effectively (i.e., articulation, pronunciation, volume, tempo, pitch, stress, gestures, eye contact, facial expression, and poise) in keeping with purpose, audience needs, and individual cultural and linguistic background.

outcomes.statement: Create a variety of informational (including an inquiry/research paper and an editorial) and literary (including a real or invented narrative and a literary criticism essay) texts that are appropriate to a variety of audiences and purposes including informing, persuading, and entertaining.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Create a variety of written communications using various elements of discourse (e.g., purpose, speaker, audience, form), in narrative, expository, persuasive, informative, and/or descriptive texts:
- Choose focus to address audience needs, stated purpose, and context
- Develop a thesis statement
- Create an organizing structure appropriate to purpose, audience, and context
- Include relevant information and exclude extraneous information
- Provide facts and details, describe or analyze subject, explain benefits or limitations, compare or contrast, or provide graphics or illustrations
- Clarify and defend positions with relevant evidence, including facts, expert opinions, quotations, and/or expressions of commonly accepted beliefs and logical reasoning
- Use a variety of rhetorical devices to support assertions (e.g., appeal to logic through reasoning, case study, and analogy)
- Anticipate potential misunderstandings, problems, or mistakes that might arise for audience
- Use appropriate format and structure drafts using standard forms and predictable structures such as headings, white space, and graphics
- Provide a coherent conclusion.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Select, use, and evaluate deliberately a wide variety of before (page 31), during (page 32), and after (page 33) strategies to communicate meaning when writing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Apply accurately and effectively the language cues and conventions (page 24) to construct and communicate meaning when writing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Prepare and write an inquiry/research paper (approximately 1,500 words in length, 5-6 pages typed, double-spaced):
- Focus on an important topic that interests self and emphasizes a specific part about the topic
- Size up the topic and include important details, facts, ideas, quotations, statistics, and other data
- Use primary and secondary sources that have been judged for their accuracy, completeness, currency, and biases
- Cite sources and avoid plagiarism
- Introduce the topic, get the reader's attention, and present the thesis statement
- Explain why the topic is important
- Arrange ideas so the reader can follow
- Include sources and a works-cited page and title page
- Conclude in a logical and interesting way, leaving the reader with something to think about.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text:
Write an editorial:
- Focus on a current issue or topic
- Identify the purpose (e.g., criticize, condemn, advise, commend, congratulate)
- Develop a thesis statement that clearly defines the issue and attends to the purpose
- Conduct research to collect evidence and to provide examples
- Craft an introduction that states the writer's view and captures the audience's attention
- Use evidence and ethical, logical arguments to support the thesis statement and purpose, and to persuade the audience
- Construct an effective conclusion related to the purpose and thesis statement.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Write a real or invented narrative:
- Introduce the character(s), the setting, and the conflict in the beginning
- Build suspense through the rising action to a high or turning point
- Resolve the conflict and create a satisfactory or reasonable conclusion in the ending
- Focus on what character(s) does, and "show" what the person does (instead of "tell") and how he or she does it
- Show character through dialogue, thoughts, and action
- Use external and internal dialogue
- Use action verbs.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Write a literary analysis and critical evaluation (print, film, new media) essay:
- Read to find out what the author said, how the writer was affected, what important issues the text made the writer think about, and what was enjoyed about it
- Read the text again to analyze how the author achieved these effects (what forms and techniques were used) and how successful the text was
- Respond to key questions (e.g., What was the author's purpose? How was it achieved? What were your reactions?)
- Use the text as evidence.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Experiment with and explore a variety of written text forms (e.g., chapter of a novel, short story, minutes of a meeting) and techniques (such as satire, tone, mood) and explain their appeal.

outcomes.statement: Assess own work for precision, clarity, and artistry.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Review and analyze own work (e.g., for content, organization, delivery, audience response, style).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify a variety of skills and strategies in viewing, listening, reading, representing, speaking, writing; and explain how the skills and strategies improve communication.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify appropriate steps to take to improve comprehension and communication skills.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Select a variety of products that most clearly reflect own growth and competencies as a communicator, and explain the reasons for the choices.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Assess the effect of new understandings and strategies on self and others.

outcomes.statement: Reflect on personal growth and successes in language learning and consider the role and importance of language learning when developing personal goals and plans as a self-directed, curious, self-appraising, and open-minded learner.

indicators.text: Review and analyze own work (e.g., for content, organization, delivery, audience response, style).

indicators.text: Identify a variety of skills and strategies in viewing, listening, reading, representing, speaking, writing; and explain how the skills and strategies improve communication.
