outcomes.statement: Explore machining as a discipline.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Introduction to Machining (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify machining as a reduction process.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the role of machining in various industries (e.g., manufacturing, forestry, mining and agriculture).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the influence of machining on everyday life (e.g., transportation and household items).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore connections between machining and other trades.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain modern changes in machining such as computer numerical control (CNC).

outcomes.statement: Explore measurement systems used in machining.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4A: Basic Measurement (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore imperial and metric systems of measurement and their uses in machining.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between semi-precision and precision measurements.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate accurate measurements to within 1/64” (0.5 mm).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform accurate measurements of angles with a protractor.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Categorize angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Calculate angles and distances using both decimals and fractions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Interpret readings from a variety of measurement tools including dials, metres and scales.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate accurate use of advanced measurement tools.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4B: Advanced Measurement (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Perform accurate measurements using Vernier and dial calipers.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Practice using various micrometers (e.g., outside, inside and depth).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate use of advanced measurement tools (e.g., telescoping gauges, gauge blocks and small hole gauges).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the accurate use of digital measurement tools to within 0.001” or 0.02 mm.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of proper care, cleaning and storage of measurement tools.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practice taking measurements with a dial indicator.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate use of dial indicators for inspection of workpieces and machine set-up.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss factors that can affect the accuracy of measurement.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore the history and impact of technology on the science of metrology.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in determining measurement standards.

outcomes.statement: Examine information found on a technical drawing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Using Technical Drawings (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss specific information found in the title block on a technical drawing (e.g., scale, name and tolerances).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify symbols used by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the use of standardized symbols, lines and figures.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the importance of geometric tolerances and dimensions (e.g., concentricity, parallelism and orientation).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Differentiate between isometric (3D) and orthographic (2D top, front and right-side views) representations.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop shop sketches of parts to be produced.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate techniques to effectively prepare materials and tools for a machining project through layout work.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Layout Work (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 4A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the value of the layout process.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the safe handling and use of layout tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of layout tools (e.g., layout dye, scriber, hermaphrodite caliper and surface gauge).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore the need to protect layout equipment from being damaged.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective use of tools for precision layout work (e.g., Vernier height gauge, right angle plate, parallels, V-blocks and straightedge).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply layout techniques using various layout and hand tools (e.g., drill grinding gauge and right-angle square) to complete a project.

outcomes.statement: Explore the use of machining tools.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Machining Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the proper use and safety considerations for machining tools (e.g., compliance with manufacturer recommended uses and limitations).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research safety guards, how they are intended to protect the worker and the worker responsibility to report issues with the guard.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Classify machining tools (e.g., lathes, drills, grinders, mills and saws) as striking, grinding, cutting or drilling tools.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the use of measurement tools (e.g., Vernier and dial calipers).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the evolution of machining tools from the industrial revolution to present day.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore connections between project material and tool selection.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate correct storage and maintenance of machining tools according to the manufacturer.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the application of computer numerical control (CNC) and advanced machining tools.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inspect tools for damage and tag for repair as instructed by the supervisor.

outcomes.statement: Develop safe and efficient hand tool technique.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Hand Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify common machine shop hand tools (e.g., files, hacksaw, ball peen hammer, chisel and screwdriver).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe work practices when working with hand tools and equipment including the use of PPE recommended by the tool manufacturer.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Maintain a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess and mitigate risks related to the use of hand tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate the selection and use of the correct tool for a specific task.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect tools for damage and tag for repair as instructed by a supervisor.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate effective maintenance, repair and cleaning of tools.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply proper hand tool techniques to produce a project.

outcomes.statement: Explore the types of fasteners used by machinists.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Fasteners (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Follow safe work practices when using fasteners, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify fasteners based on specifications such as metric/SAE (e.g., Unified National Coarse [UNC], Unified National Fine [UNF]), grade, length, diameter and thread pitch or count.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Decode the nomenclature associated with threaded fasteners.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the application of fasteners including pins, rivets, keys and self-locking tapers.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate tools to manipulate fasteners.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore how adhesives and sealants are used as fasteners and how some are not compatible if mixed.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the need for safe, proper handling of adhesives.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the importance of tightening sequence and torque values of specific fasteners.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Utilize torque wrenches to properly tighten fasteners.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Complete thread repair of damaged fasteners using a tap and die set.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate tools to extract broken fasteners.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe the use of commercially available products to assist with the removal (e.g., penetrating oil) or securing of fasteners (e.g., Loctite).

outcomes.statement: Examine the characteristics of metals used in machining.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Metal Characteristics (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore different classifications of metals (e.g., ferrous, nonferrous, plain carbon steel, alloy steel).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss mechanical properties of metals (e.g., hardness, toughness, ductility, colouration and resistance to corrosion).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with metals.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze characteristics of specific metals using non-destructive and destructive testing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify typical uses of different types of metals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research material costs for a given project.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) material classification system (e.g., 1018, 4140 and stainless 316).

outcomes.statement: Investigate the purpose of heat treatment of metals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Heat Treatment of Metals (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the reasons for heat-treating metals.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the properties and characteristics of metals that can be heat-treated.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Demonstrate heat treatment on a sample or project material.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when heat-treating metals.

outcomes.statement: Examine surface finishing techniques and their applications.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Metal Finishing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how the finish of a machined surface is designated using a set of numbers and symbols indicating roughness.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the relationship between the quality of a machined surface and production costs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of surface finish with respect to application.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify potential hazards associated with finishing processes and tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate finishing techniques (e.g., polishing, lapping, grinding and filing).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine speeds and feeds of typical machining tools as they relate to required surface finish.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Compare completed project with samples of surface finishes.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when finishing metal.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Apply appropriate finishing techniques to achieve specific surface finishes.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore inorganic coatings used in finishing metals.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate safe and effective use of jigs and fixtures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Jigs and Fixtures (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify specific applications for jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how to use jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Design a simple jig to guide a drill bit to create a hole or assist with a project.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design a simple fixture to be used with a lathe, grinder or drill press.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with jigs and fixtures.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore industrial efficiencies created by using jigs and fixtures.

outcomes.statement: Explore safe and effective use of cutting fluids.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14: Cutting Fluids (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe working practices, storage and disposal of cutting fluids.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the purpose of cutting fluids.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Review the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for each cutting fluid.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the properties and function of cutting fluids.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare samples of various cutting fluids.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the properties of cutting oils and water-soluble coolants.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research industrial applications of cutting fluids.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the safe and effective operation of drilling machines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Drills and Drilling Machines (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the styles and types of drilling machines.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Review safety rules, including the effective use of personal protective equipment (PPE), that must be followed while using drilling machines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the parts of a drill press.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Practice using appropriate devices (e.g., jigs and fixtures) to hold material.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the various operations (e.g., drilling, countersinking, counterboring, reaming and spot-facing) that can be performed using a drill press.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Calculate and adjust spindle speed revolutions per minute (rpm) and feed rate.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with drilling machines.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Conduct maintenance of equipment, including inspecting and sharpening drill bits.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explore industrial applications of drilling machines.

outcomes.statement: Investigate safe and effective use of saws and cutoff machines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Saws and Cutoff Machines (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List various types of saws and cutoff machines (e.g., horizontal band, vertical band and abrasive cutoff).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore safety procedures for safe and effective use of saws and cutoff machines.

indicators.label: c

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III - Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act,2019:
- the right to know - the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate - in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse - work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?

outcomes.statement: Analyze the relationship between marketing and business or organizational success.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Introduction to Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the areas that marketing entails beyond selling and advertising.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss who (e.g., businesses, government, school teams or clubs and notfor-profits) might engage in marketing and their reasons for doing so.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between commercial (i.e., for a fictitious or real-life brand) or social (i.e., for behaviour change around a social issue) marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify examples of commercial (e.g., Saskatchewan Roughriders) and social (e.g., ending mental health stigma or promoting the use of seatbelts) marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the concepts of brand and branding and the relationship between branding and marketing.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the relationship between satisfying consumers and meeting organizational goals (e.g., profit or changed behaviour).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss strategies (e.g., communicating, exceeding expectations, asking for feedback and showing appreciation) for building good customer relationships and creating value for consumers.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Relate marketing to competing effectively, much like a sports team plays to its strengths.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Summarize reasons (e.g., importance to business or organizational success, career opportunities and being an informed consumer) for studying marketing.

outcomes.statement: Examine factors that impact a business or organization’s marketing activities.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: The Marketing Environment (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe what is meant by the marketing environment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine forces (i.e., demographic, socio-cultural, economic, technological, competitive and regulatory) that influence the marketing environment.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Research the purpose of, and ways to conduct, an environmental scan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Assess the current state of demographic, socio-cultural, economic, technological and regulatory forces locally, provincially, nationally and globally for a variety of products.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Predict the future impact of demographic, socio-cultural, economic, technological and regulatory forces on marketing activities for the same products.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of understanding and constantly monitoring the marketing environment for successful and effective marketing.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the relationship between consumer behaviour and marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Consumer Behaviour (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of understanding consumer behaviour for effective and successful marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discover how and why consumer behaviour can change over time.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship among Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, consumer behaviour and marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the five stages (i.e., problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, purchase decision and post-purchase behaviour) of the purchase decision process that a consumer goes through in making purchasing decisions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on personal experiences with the purchase decision process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Examine factors that influence consumer buying behaviour including:
- situational (e.g., reason for making a purchase; social surroundings such as others present at the time of purchase; physical surroundings such as background music, decor and crowding; the time of day or amount of time the consumer has available; timing of the purchase [e.g., last-minute]; and the consumer’s mood);
- psychological (e.g., motivation, personality, perception, lifestyle, attitudes and beliefs); and,
- socio-cultural (e.g., word of mouth and opinion leaders; reference groups such as family, friends, celebrities or athletes; culture and subcultures).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify examples of referral marketing (e.g., Uber share codes or refer a friend promotions).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the concept of buyer’s remorse and its potential impact on both buyers and the sellers.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research ways (e.g., a coupon towards a future purchase, loyalty cards/programs and money-back guarantee) marketers attempt to reduce buyer’s remorse.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the components of the AIDA model including Attention, Interest, Desire and Action.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Relate the AIDA model to marketing strategies that capitalize on consumer behaviour.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on ways that consumer behaviour can affect individuals as well as others in all aspects of life (e.g., at home, at work, at play and at school).

outcomes.statement: Analyze strategies for successfully creating, marketing and managing a brand.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Successful Brands (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the concept of a brand.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between brand identity and brand image.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of a strong brand image and a brand identity that resonates with consumers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the characteristics of a purpose-driven brand, including its potential impact on consumer behaviour.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain personal reasons for identifying with, and finding inspiration from, specific brands.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the concept of brand positioning.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify types of brand positioning strategies such as cost-driven positioning, niche product positioning or quality of service positioning.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the brand positioning strategies used by a variety of successful brands such as the Saskatchewan Roughriders.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the concept of brand extension.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Provide real-life examples of brand extensions (e.g., a tech brand such as Apple adding watches to its product line).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine the concept of brand personality and the emotional response it intends to elicit in consumers.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on personal experiences with, and responses to, brand personalities.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Describe the concept of brand voice.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Identify real-life examples of brand voice used in the marketing of a variety of products.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Describe the concept of brand relationship.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Examine strategies for building strong brand relationships with customers including community building.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of a brand recognizing, and differentiating itself from, competitors.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Justify the importance of effective online reputation management (ORM).

indicators.label: s
indicators.text: Propose strategies (e.g., answering promptly to online feedback/comments, encouraging satisfied customers to submit online reviews and owning up to mistakes) for effective and successful ORM.

indicators.label: t
indicators.text: Research instances when a brand’s reputation was damaged including the reasons for the reputational damage, the brand’s response and the resulting outcome.

outcomes.statement: Examine personal branding.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Personal Branding (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe personal branding.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the components (e.g., who one is, what one stands for, the values one embraces and the ways in which one expresses those values) of a personal brand.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify elements (e.g., authenticity and consistency) of a successful personal brand.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss how a personal brand can be impacted by online behaviour, including social media use.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on one’s personal brand including brand identity, image and voice.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Create a self-representation that depicts one’s personal brand and share it with a trusted friend, adult or family member.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between personal and professional branding.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recommend ways to establish and build a positive personal brand.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the personal brand of at least one individual considered to be personally inspirational.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Research instances when personal brands have been negatively impacted and the reasons for each situation.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a plan for maintaining or building one’s personal brand.

outcomes.statement: Investigate components of the traditional marketing mix.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: The Traditional Marketing Mix (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the elements of the traditional marketing mix, also known as the 4 Ps (i.e., product, price, place and promotion).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the application of the traditional marketing mix to a social marketing campaign.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between products that are tangible (e.g., goods) and intangible (e.g., services, ideas or experiences).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Categorize local businesses or organizations according to the types of products they offer.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss reasons (e.g., meeting a basic need or contributing to a desired lifestyle) why customers purchase a particular product.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the importance of offering a product that meets or exceeds customer expectations.

indicators.label: g
h
indicators.text: Assess the effects of pricing a product too high or pricing it too low.

indicators.label: i
j
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of offering a product in the right place and at the right time.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text:
Research considerations for product placement, such as:
- where potential customers are located;
- where and how potential customers shop (e.g., retail location and online); and,
- where the competition places their products.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine the role of promotion in gaining the attention of consumers and motivating them to take action (e.g., purchase a product or change behaviour).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Identify paid (e.g., radio or television advertisements, print media and social advertisements) and free (e.g., organic social media and word of mouth) promotional opportunities.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Compare features of push and pull marketing.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Identify real-life examples of push and pull marketing.

indicators.label: p
q
indicators.text: Investigate advantages (e.g., global reach, cost efficiency and measurable results) and disadvantages (e.g., security and privacy issues, timeconsuming, and skills and training required) of online promotion.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Examine the application of the 4 Ps for a business, organization or brand/product of personal interest.

outcomes.statement: Investigate components of the extended marketing mix.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6B: The Extended Marketing Mix (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the three additional Ps (i.e., people, process and physical evidence) that have been added to the traditional marketing mix to create the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the reasons (e.g., easier to apply to services and the advent of online marketing and e-commerce) for the creation of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe various roles (e.g., salesperson, marketing team and customer service representative) that are considered part of the people element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss desirable characteristics (e.g., effective and perceived positively by customers) associated with people roles in the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the role of brand voice in the people “P” of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on personal or observed positive and negative people experiences as a customer.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the process element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research desirable characteristics (e.g., efficiency, reliability and sustainability) of effective processes in the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify examples (e.g., packaging, websites, and branding such as logos on employee uniforms and awards) associated with the physical evidence element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the application of the extended marketing mix for a major global brand.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the use of digital and traditional marketing strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Digital and Traditional Promotion (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between traditional (e.g., print, television, direct mail and outdoor advertising such as signage) and digital marketing (i.e., online).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify visible applications of traditional and digital marketing within the community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Relate traditional and digital marketing to the promotion “P” in the marketing mix.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess advantages and disadvantages associated with traditional and digital marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between user behaviour (i.e., of the target audience) to the selection and application of traditional and/or digital marketing strategies.

indicators.label: f
g
indicators.text: Assess the impact on marketing strategies of limitations (e.g., blocking of cookies) imposed by digital platforms.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the use and impact of animation and video in modern marketing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Defend the use of traditional, digital, or a hybrid of both types of marketing for a variety of given marketing scenarios.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify ways that consumer behaviour (e.g., online or through SMS) can be tracked and leveraged for marketing purposes.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine the types of consumer information that can be tracked through digital marketing.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Debate the ethics of tracking and leveraging consumer behaviour for marketing purposes.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Describe the concept of advertising avoidance.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss actions (e.g., not sharing information, blocking pop-up advertisements on the computer and unsubscribing from newsletters) that consumers can take to avoid viewing or receiving advertising.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Propose ways in which marketers can effectively deal with consumer advertising avoidance.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Investigate the origins, evolution and impact of influencer marketing to the present day.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the process for becoming, and succeeding as, an influencer marketer.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Propose marketing strategies that may be effective to reach consumers of the future.

indicators.label: s
indicators.text: Develop a plan for promoting a business, brand or product of personal choice as an influencer marketer.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of market research for successful and effective marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Market Research (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and importance of ongoing market research for effective and successful marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the correlation between market research and the ability to make sound business or operational decisions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the importance of identifying and monitoring the competition as part of initial and ongoing market research.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define qualitative and quantitative research.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe ways in which qualitative and quantitative research might be conducted and how the results might be used in marketing research.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between primary and secondary market research.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify ways (e.g., observations and surveys such as pop-up or omnibus) in which primary data can be gathered.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages (e.g., less costly than primary research and easier/quicker to gather) and disadvantages (e.g., datedness and reason for collecting may not align with one’s purposes) of secondary research.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Identify sources of secondary data such as:
- government departments, libraries, business incubators and chambers of commerce (public and generally free);
- trade associations and research firms (commercial and generally associated with subscription or association fees); and,
- colleges, universities, technical institutes (academic).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Describe ways to confirm the credibility of sources of secondary data as well as the accuracy of that data.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explain the concept of a target market.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe what market segmentation is and why it is beneficial.

indicators.label: m
n
indicators.text: Investigate how marketers use buyer personas to drive marketing success.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Outline the steps for creating a buyer persona.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Develop several buyer personas, including one for self.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Describe marketing strategies that would be effective with potential customers, including self, for a variety of products.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of ethical and socially responsible behaviour and marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Ethics and Social Responsibility (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define ethics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Describe good ethics in business as it relates to relationships between, but not limited to:
- businesses and customers;
- businesses and suppliers; and,
- employers and employees.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess the importance of regulations for both consumers and businesses.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the evolution and resulting impact of privacy and consumer protection laws on marketing practices in Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the importance of ethical behaviour and business ethics as they relate to ethical marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify examples of types of false or misleading advertising such as bait and switch, price deception, unsubstantiated claims and misleading photos or illustrations.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Summarize the standards for marketing in Canada as detailed by the Canadian Marketing Association Code of Ethics and Standards.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship among purpose-driven marketing, ethics and social responsibility.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Examine social responsibility and the benefits (e.g., to the business, consumer, society, the environment and others) of having a socially responsible marketing strategy.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze the impact of marketing strategies used by local, provincial (e.g., tentree), national (e.g., Manitobah Mukluks) and international (e.g., The Body Shop, Toms, and Proctor and Gamble—Dawn Soap) companies that promote themselves as being socially responsible.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research ways (e.g., Certified B Corporations) to verify a company’s claim of being socially responsible.

outcomes.statement: Examine the importance of inclusive marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Inclusive Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 4, 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe inclusive marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain accessible marketing as a component of inclusive marketing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research ways that marketing content can be more easily accessed by users of all abilities (e.g., audio or larger text for individuals with vision impairments, print for individuals with hearing impairments and digital content for individuals with motor impairments) or by users with limited access (e.g., print materials or television content for individuals with no or limited access to the Internet).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the impact that inclusive marketing can have on a brand (e.g., creating loyalty and trust) and on others (e.g., giving voice to a marginalized group).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of cultural understanding in developing effective and culturally sensitive marketing content.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between cultural appropriation and cultural appreciation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the potential impact of using cultural appropriation and cultural appreciation in marketing campaigns.

indicators.label: h
i
indicators.text: Explain, and provide examples of, stereotype marketing.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Justify stereotype marketing as an exclusive, rather than inclusive, marketing strategy.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Brainstorm examples (e.g., a dad making dinner or a mom fixing a lawn mower) of marketing that challenge stereotypes.

outcomes.statement: Examine the relationship between marketing and customer experiences.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Customer Experience Marketing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between customer service and customer experiences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain what customer-centric marketing means and the importance of a business or organization knowing and understanding its customers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the benefits (e.g., greater brand loyalty and improved customer retention) of such marketing efforts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of monitoring, managing and responding to online and other reviews.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Propose strategies for replying to both positive and negative online reviews.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the stages (e.g., pre-purchase, purchase and post-purchase) of a customer journey map.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore effective marketing strategies for connecting with consumers at each of the stages.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal encounters with poor and exemplary customer experiences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe characteristics of ideal customer experiences.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess the role that marketers play in creating and supporting the ideal customer experience through customer experience marketing.

outcomes.statement: Investigate careers in marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Careers in Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 1, 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research opportunities and trends in marketing careers in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the marketing services offered by a variety of Saskatchewan-based marketing or advertising companies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities typically required by those who work in marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Generate a list of questions to ask a professional in the marketing industry to learn about their work; questions may include:
- What do you do?
- What knowledge and skills do you use every day?
- What does a typical day look like for you?
- What is the most interesting marketing project you have worked on?

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: List personal interests, skills, abilities and traits that may lead to a career in marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research which marketing occupations are facing shortages and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally and/or provincially.

indicators.label: g
h

outcomes.statement: Examine the benefits of a positive health and safety culture in the marketing workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Health and Safety in the Marketing Workplace (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the impact of a workplace injury on the injured and others including the employer, work colleagues, family and friends.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Describe the importance and benefits of a positive health and safety culture at work.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define a workplace hazard.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential physical hazards (e.g., exposure to allergens such as perfumes and other scents, sitting for long periods of time and eye strain) associated with office work.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research causes of stress and anxiety (e.g., little or no results from a marketing campaign and time pressures) for those working in marketing careers.

indicators.label: g
h
i
indicators.text: Compare the hazards associated with working remotely to working in an office environment.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain why some brands align themselves with safety messaging such as Mission Zero.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a marketing campaign that promotes a positive health and safety culture in the marketing workplace.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on personal and collective responsibility for, and commitment to, developing and supporting a positive health and safety culture at work.

outcomes.statement: Examine characteristics and components of a strategic marketing plan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: Strategic Marketing Plan A (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 6A or 6B, 7, 8, 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain a value proposition.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify examples of value propositions presented by several brands.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between a value proposition and strategic marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the importance and interrelatedness of the marketing mix (i.e., traditional or extended) for strategic marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research tenets of an effective marketing campaign such as consistency (e.g., of message, brand, tone and relevancy), frequency (e.g., of message; less effective advertisements require more frequency) and creativity (e.g., amusing; engaging; and featuring well-designed imagery, video or text).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of a marketing plan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess characteristics (e.g., organized, easy to read, clear section headings and free of grammar or spelling errors) of prepared strategic marketing plans.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze the impact of finances on a marketing plan.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Describe the elements of prepared marketing plans, such as:
- market analysis (e.g., purpose and mission of the business or organization; description of current markets and strategies; primary competitors; and SWOT [i.e., strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats] analysis);
- marketing strategy (e.g., goals and expected outcomes, target market description, marketing mix); and,
- implementation (e.g., activity schedule including responsibilities, schedule and budget; evaluation procedures including evidence of success and methods of collecting the evidence).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify reasons for changing or recalibrating a marketing plan.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a commercial or social marketing plan with a budgetary limit.

outcomes.statement: Develop, implement, manage and evaluate the success of a marketing campaign.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14B: Strategic Marketing Plan B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research companies and organizations (e.g., local businesses, not-forprofits and school or community clubs and teams) as potential clients or beneficiaries for a marketing campaign.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess the pros and cons of the various companies and organizations researched to determine the best option(s) for a project.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze marketing strategies used by companies and organizations that are considered competitors.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Collaborate with the chosen company or organization to develop a marketing plan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Implement the marketing plan.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Monitor the implementation of the marketing plan and make adjustments, as required, throughout the process.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conclude and evaluate the success of the marketing campaign based upon the criteria outlined in the marketing plan.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal contributions to, and personal growth resulting from, developing, implementing, managing and evaluating the marketing campaign.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know – the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate – in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a work placement experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 81: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 80

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply relevant skills and abilities during the work placement experience.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Document knowledge and awareness of employment standards, safety, workplace ethics, rights and responsibilities, occupational health and safety, and networking observed during the work placement.

outcomes.statement: Relate one’s work placement experience to personal and career goals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 82: Work Study Follow-up (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 81

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Reflect on the attainment of personal and learning goals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Update personal career documentation (e.g., resume, portfolio) following the work placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Prepare a letter, note, card or other communication for the work placement employer, expressing appreciation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and/or revise personal and career goals based on the work placement experience.

outcomes.statement: Develop an awareness of the automotive industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Automotive Industry (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the history of the automobile and automotive industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and explain the operation of an automobile’s major systems (e.g., steering, suspension, brakes, drive train, cooling, lubrication, engine).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe processes used to identify automotive system faults.

outcomes.statement: Perform common automotive diagnosis and repair processes.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Automotive Diagnosis and Repair Processes (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when performing automotive diagnosis and repair, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common practices and procedures involved in automotive repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify steps (e.g., identify, diagnose, repair and confirm the repair) common to automotive diagnostic processes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use appropriate service information to identify proper repair processes for a specific problem.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify required components, and compile a parts list and cost estimate, for a specific repair or modification process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of preventive maintenance of an automobile.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conduct a visual inspection of an automobile, including tire pressure and condition, lights, fluid levels, condition of hoses, belts and battery.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the automotive workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Automotive Safety Equipment, Hazardous Materials, and Housekeeping Skills (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the importance of safety when undertaking automotive service procedures, including safety hazards and preventative measures common to the automotive industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage as a result of unsafe work acts or environments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect and utilize protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE), such as safety goggles, hearing protection, gloves and footwear, and appropriate PPE cleaning procedures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential health concerns when PPE is not used properly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the correct fire extinguisher for different classifications (i.e., A, B, C, D and K) of fires and how to use the extinguisher correctly (i.e., PASS - Pull Aim Squeeze Sweep).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean workplace and methods used to maintain a clean workplace.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Locate, identify and explain the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station and first aid station) in the workplace.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify, label, store and handle hazardous materials according to Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS 2015).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices, including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate safe procedures to lift and support vehicles.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Vehicle Lifting and Support (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow appropriate safe practices related to lifting and supporting vehicles, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify appropriate lifting and support equipment needed for the task.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify lift and balance points for different types of vehicles.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Position vehicles safely and correctly before lifting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Lift and lower vehicles in a safe manner using floor jacks and jack stands.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Raise large drivetrain assemblies using hoists and transmission jacks.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Lift and lower vehicles on a hoist in a safe manner using proper procedures.

outcomes.statement: Explore factors to consider related to vehicle purchase.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Vehicle Purchase (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare a budget prior to purchasing a vehicle.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between personal wants and needs based on a specific budget.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss factors (e.g., environmental impact of a vehicle, the cost of operations and potential repair costs) to consider when purchasing a vehicle.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify vehicles that fit criteria based on personal budget, wants and needs.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze potential vehicles for purchase based on customer, commercial and technical reviews.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain and/or perform procedures for inspecting and testing vehicles before purchase.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify safety practices to follow when inspecting and testing vehicles.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Estimate potential repair costs of any service or repair needed for a used vehicle.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain insurance, financing and warranty options for purchasing or leasing a new or used vehicle.

outcomes.statement: Locate automotive service information utilizing appropriate sources.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Automotive Service Information (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the type of information available from common automotive service information sources (e.g., manuals, computers, scan tools, diagnostic charts, technical bulletins and apps).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine correct service information such as torque specifications, wiring diagrams and disassembly/assembly procedures from appropriate sources.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate care in handling manuals, computers and scan tools.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze vehicle identification numbers (VIN) and compliance labels.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain hand and power tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Hand and Power Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with hand and power tools, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Classify tools according to their capabilities (e.g., cutting, striking and holding) and method of power (e.g., hand, power, electric and hydraulic).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Maintain and store tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize that metric and imperial systems of measurement are both used in the automotive industry.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify, select and use appropriate tools for specific tasks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect tools before use and tag for repair as required.

outcomes.statement: Identify, select and use automotive fasteners properly.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Automotive Fasteners (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with automotive fasteners, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common categories (e.g., clips, pins, nuts, bolts, washers, screws and rivets) of automotive fasteners.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify fasteners based on specifications such as metric/SAE, grade, length, diameter and thread pitch.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe types (e.g., hex, 12 point and Torx) of fastener heads commonly found in automotive applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and use appropriate tools to manipulate fasteners.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of torqueing fasteners, including following a fastener tightening sequence.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair differentials.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25: Differentials (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., lift and support components properly and be aware of component weight and pinch points) when working with differentials, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the function and operation (e.g., power flow, differentiation and limited slip) of differentials.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform differential service and repairs, such as changing fluid, removing and replacing differentials, overhauling and inspecting.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive storage batteries.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26: Automotive Storage Batteries (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of battery acid, overheating and gas emissions) when working with automotive storage batteries, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Follow appropriate procedures for disposing of automotive storage batteries.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the construction and operation of common types (e.g., lead acid, gel cell, absorbent glass mat [AGM]) of automotive storage batteries.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify battery ratings, such as cold cranking amperes (CCA) and reserve capacity minutes.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Test (e.g., check voltage and load test) and service batteries.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Follow appropriate connection order when performing battery replacement, charging and boosting operations.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose common battery failures such as frozen, sulfated and open or short circuits.

outcomes.statement: Explore the function and operation of automotive electrical systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27A: Fundamentals of Automotive Electricity and Electronics (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., grounding static electricity, being aware of high voltage electric drives, avoiding lead solder fumes and connecting batteries correctly) when working with automotive electrical systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe major electrical concepts, including atomic structure, insulators, conductors and semi-conductors.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between voltage, resistance, current and their units of measurement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify factors (e.g., length, diameter, material, temperature, connection quality and corrosion) that affect resistance and their effect on current and voltage.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify various sources of voltage (e.g., electro-chemical, thermal electric, piezo electric and photo electric) in automotive settings.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply Ohm’s law and the power equation to electrical circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Differentiate between the characteristics of series, parallel and seriesparallel electric circuits.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform electrical repairs by splicing, soldering, taping and/or using heat shrink tubing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the quality of electrical repairs.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive electrical systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27B: Advanced Automotive Electricity and Electronics (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-30 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 27A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., grounding static electricity, being aware of high voltage electric drives, avoiding lead solder fumes and connecting batteries correctly) when working with automotive electrical systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common electrical and electronic components in automotive circuits.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and select appropriate wire gauge, connectors and circuit protection devices (e.g., fuses and breakers).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Interpret electrical system wiring diagrams (e.g., lighting, horns, windows and doors) to help diagnose electrical problems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform common electrical tests (e.g., voltage, voltage drop, resistance, current and parasitic draw) using electrical testing equipment such as multimeters and test lights.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Provide examples of common faults (e.g., short to ground, short circuit, high resistance, open circuit and mechanical resistance) that may occur in automotive electrical circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common automotive electrical faults using appropriate diagnostic techniques.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Perform mechanical adjustments (e.g., headlight, camera, sensor and switch alignments) to automotive electrical system components.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive charging systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28: Automotive Charging Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 27A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., disconnect battery and prevent grounding of live wires) when working with automotive charging systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and locate the components (e.g., alternator, voltage regulator and battery) of an automotive charging system.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how the principles of electromagnetic induction apply to alternators.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of automotive charging systems and their components.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify common symptoms and faults associated with automotive charging systems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment to test automotive charging systems.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common automotive charging system faults such as alternator failure, loose or damaged belts and poor connections.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive starting systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29: Automotive Starting Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 27A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., disconnect battery and prevent grounding of live wires) when working with automotive starting systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and locate the components (e.g., battery, starter motor, solenoid, ignition switch and starter relay) of a typical automotive starting system.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how the principles of electromagnetism apply to automotive starting systems.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of automotive starting systems and their components.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the operation of starter activation and drive mechanisms.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the common symptoms and faults associated with automotive starting system malfunctions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment to test automotive starting systems.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common automotive starting system faults such as starter failure, control circuit failure and poor connections.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive ignition systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 30: Automotive Ignition Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 27A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of hot components and high voltage shock hazards) when working with automotive ignition systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the construction and operation of distributor-based and nondistributor based automotive ignition systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify common symptoms and faults with automotive ignition systems.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment to test automotive ignition systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform common automotive ignition system scheduled maintenance such as replacing spark plugs, plug wires and boots.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common automotive ignition system faults such as faulty spark plugs, wires, coils and connections.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair fuel delivery systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31: Fuel Delivery Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., handle and store fuel safely and be aware of pressurized fuel and fire hazards such as fuel ignition from hot components) when working with fuel delivery systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the operation of fuel delivery systems (e.g., mechanical, electric return and electric returnless) from tank to engine.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment to test fuel delivery systems.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform common fuel delivery system scheduled maintenance such as changing fuel filters and system flushes.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common fuel delivery system faults such as faulty filters, clogged injectors, leak repair, tank removal and pump replacement.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair emission control systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 32: Emission Control Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of hot surfaces and ensure appropriate ventilation) when working with emission control systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and function of emission control systems (e.g., EVAP, catalytic converter, EGR and PCV).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Test emission control systems using appropriate equipment to ensure proper operation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common emission control faults such as plugged converters, open EVAP lines and gas cap seal issues.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair passenger restraint systems.

indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., torqueing fasteners to specification) when working with passenger restraint systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the construction and operation of various passenger restraint systems (e.g., seat belts and their recoils and car seats).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment to test passenger restraint systems.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inspect passenger restraint system components for common faults such as frayed belts, retractor failure and cracked or broken buckles.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Install passenger restraint system components (e.g., child car seats, bucket seats and seatbelt mechanisms).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair passenger restraint systems.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive computer systems.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of static electricity discharge, shock hazard, pinch points and hot components) when working with automotive computer systems and their components, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how automotive computers (e.g., PCM, TCM and BCM) receive, store and process information to make decisions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the relationships that exist between inputs (e.g., O2, MAP, MAF, speed and weight sensors) and outputs (e.g., injectors, IAC, ignition coil, warning lights and braking solenoids) of automotive computer managed systems (e.g., engine, transmission, body, ABS and passenger restraint).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the construction and operation of computer controlled fuel and ignition systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Retrieve and interpret computer codes and data stored in the memory of automotive computers.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment (e.g., graphing multimeter, scope, scan tools, graphing scan tools, AVR tester and noid lights) to test automotive computer systems.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform repairs to automotive computer systems following appropriate test procedures.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use appropriate equipment to test and diagnose electric and/or hybrid vehicles.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use appropriate procedures to repair electric and/or hybrid vehicles.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the development of electric and hybrid vehicles, including different types of hybrid drive systems.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.
